docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Conduit

Publish 13 sensors of your iPhone, iPad or Mac to ROS 2: camera, LiDAR, IMU, GPS and more, over Zenoh or DDS, with no bridge.

Download on the App Store Connect with a QR code

Downloaded over 10,000 times. Ranked as high as #4 in Developer Tools on the Japanese App Store.

ros2 topic list
  1. /conduit/audio
  2. /conduit/barometer
  3. /conduit/battery_state
  4. /conduit/camera/wide/image_raw/compressed
  5. /conduit/fix
  6. /conduit/illuminance
  7. /conduit/imu
  8. /conduit/joy
  9. /conduit/magnetic_field
  10. /conduit/points
  11. /conduit/pose
  12. /conduit/range
  13. /conduit/temperature
  14. /tf
  15. /tf_static

Conduit publishes the sensors of your Apple device to a ROS 2 graph over Zenoh or DDS. No bridge, no rcl / rclcpp, nothing to build on the device. Scan a QR code from your ROS 2 PC and the topics show up in ros2 topic list. Conduit has been downloaded over 10,000 times and has ranked as high as #4 in Developer Tools on the Japanese App Store.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text:
1. Install Conduit from the App Store.
  2. On your ROS 2 PC (Ubuntu, RHEL or Fedora, with ROS 2 sourced), run: 
    curl -fsSL https://conduit.direct/pair.sh | bash
    The script checks the setup and shows a QR code.
  3. Scan the QR code with the iPhone's Camera app. Conduit opens and fills in the connection settings.
  4. Turn on sensors and tap Start, then check on the PC: 
    ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu

QR pairing needs Conduit 2.6.0 or later. See Connect with a QR code for the requirements, Tailscale and troubleshooting.

Set up by hand: Zenoh
  1. Start the Zenoh router on your ROS 2 PC: 
    source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash   # or jazzy / humble / …
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0  # 0-232
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd
  2. In Conduit, open Settings: Transport Zenoh, Router Address the PC's IP, Router Port 7447, Domain ID the same as the PC, and Distribution your ROS 2 release (Lyrical for new installs). Tap Done.
  3. Turn on sensors and tap Start.
  4. Check: ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu
Set up by hand: DDS (CycloneDDS)
  1. On your ROS 2 PC, add the iPhone as a discovery peer and restart the ROS 2 daemon: 
    source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash   # or jazzy / humble / …
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0  # 0-232
export CYCLONEDDS_URI='<CycloneDDS><Domain><Discovery><Peers><Peer address="IPHONE_IP"/></Peers></Discovery></Domain></CycloneDDS>'
ros2 daemon stop
    Settings → Discovery → This Device in Conduit shows the iPhone's address.
  2. In Conduit, open Settings: Transport DDS, Domain ID the same as the PC, Distribution your ROS 2 release. In Discovery, add the PC's IP under Peers and pick en0 (WiFi) as the Network Interface. Tap Done.
  3. Turn on sensors and tap Start.
  4. Check: ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu --qos-reliability best_effort

Run ros2 daemon stop again whenever you change RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID or CYCLONEDDS_URI: the daemon keeps its first settings. See Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Zenoh router (Docker)
docs.text:
Pre-built images on ghcr.io: 

# ROS 2 Lyrical
docker run -d -p 7447:7447 --name ros_lyrical_zenoh ghcr.io/youtalk/conduit-support:lyrical
# ROS 2 Jazzy
docker run -d -p 7447:7447 --name ros_jazzy_zenoh ghcr.io/youtalk/conduit-support:jazzy
# ROS 2 Humble
docker run -d -p 7447:7447 --name ros_humble_zenoh ghcr.io/youtalk/conduit-support:humble

Or with Docker Compose: 

git clone https://github.com/youtalk/conduit-support.git
cd conduit-support/docker

# Default domain ID (0)
docker compose up ros-lyrical -d

# Custom domain ID via .env (recommended for persistence)
echo "ROS_DOMAIN_ID=5" > .env
docker compose up ros-lyrical -d

# Or override per-invocation
ROS_DOMAIN_ID=5 docker compose up ros-lyrical -d

# Stop
docker compose down

docs.title: DDS subscriber (Docker, Linux only)
docs.text:
macOS note: Docker Desktop on macOS does not provide true host networking, so the container cannot receive DDS traffic from an iPhone on the same LAN. On macOS, run your DDS subscriber natively or in a Parallels/UTM VM.

cd conduit-support/docker
echo "ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0" > .env
docker compose -f compose-dds.yml up ros-lyrical-dds -d

# Verify
docker exec -it ros_lyrical_dds bash
source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash
ros2 topic list
ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu --qos-reliability best_effort

See docker/README.md for the complete Docker guide.

docs.title: Built on swift-ros2
docs.text: All of Conduit's ROS 2 work (Zenoh and DDS transports, the CDR codec, the Humble to Rolling wire formats, publishers and subscriptions) is done by swift-ros2, a native Swift client library for ROS 2 that started inside Conduit. To put ROS 2 in your own Swift app, use swift-ros2 directly: it runs on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Mac Catalyst and visionOS, and builds from source on Linux, Windows and Android.

docs.title: How do I connect with a QR code?
docs.text:
Requires Conduit 2.6.0 or later.

Run one command on your ROS 2 PC:

curl -fsSL https://conduit.direct/pair.sh | bash

The script checks the PC's ROS 2 setup, shows a QR code, and waits. Scan the code with the iPhone's Camera app, and Conduit fills in the connection settings. This is the easiest way to connect, for Zenoh and for DDS. See Connect with a QR code for the requirements and for what to do when nothing happens after the scan.

The manual steps below still work if you prefer them or cannot run the script.

docs.title: Which transport should I use: Zenoh or DDS?
docs.text:
Conduit supports two transports. Choose based on your ROS 2 middleware:

Zenoh DDS (CycloneDDS) RMW rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_cyclonedds_cpp Router required Yes (rmw_zenohd) No Network TCP to the router Multicast on the LAN, plus unicast to any peers you add Distros Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical, Rolling Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical, Rolling Setup Enter the router address in Settings Optional peers in Settings → Discovery

Recommendation: Use Zenoh if you already have rmw_zenoh_cpp set up. Use DDS if your stack uses rmw_cyclonedds_cpp and you don't want to run a router.

See transports.md for a deeper side-by-side comparison and network-requirements reference.

docs.title: I used Conduit 1.x — what changed in 2.0?
docs.text:
Transport choice: 2.0 adds DDS (CycloneDDS) alongside Zenoh. Your Zenoh router setup keeps working. Pick DDS in Settings → Transport.

Supported distros: Kilted and Rolling joined Humble and Jazzy in 2.0; Lyrical joined in 2.3.0 and is the default for new installs.

docs.title: How do I connect via Zenoh?
docs.text:
The QR code fills in these settings for you. To set them by hand:

  1. Start the Zenoh router on your ROS 2 system: 

    source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash   # or your distro
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0  # Set domain ID (0-232, default: 0)
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd

  2. Find your ROS 2 system's IP address: 

    ip addr show  # Linux
ifconfig      # macOS
ipconfig      # Windows

  3. In the Conduit app:

  4. Tap Settings (gear icon)
  5. Transport: Zenoh
  6. Enter Router Address (e.g., 192.168.1.100)
  7. Enter Router Port (default: 7447)
  8. Enter Domain ID (must match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on host)
  9. Distribution: your host's ROS 2 release (Lyrical by default)

  10. Tap Done. Settings are saved as you change them.

  11. Enable sensors and tap Play

Important: Domain ID must match between the app and ROS 2 system. Valid range: 0-232 (RTPS specification limit).

docs.title: How do I connect via DDS?
docs.text:
The QR code fills in these settings for you and can add the iPhone as a peer on the PC. To set them by hand:

  1. On your ROS 2 system: 
    source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash   # or your distro
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0  # Valid range: 0-232

# Restart the cached ros2 daemon so it picks up the new RMW.
# Skip this on a fresh shell where the daemon hasn't started yet.
ros2 daemon stop
ros2 daemon start          # optional — `ros2 topic list` autostarts it

ros2 topic list  # Verify the RMW is active (no topics expected yet)

Re-run ros2 daemon stop whenever you change RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, CYCLONEDDS_URI, or the unicast peer list. The daemon caches the first context it saw and silently ignores later env-var changes — symptoms include ros2 topic list showing topics from the wrong domain, missing the iOS topics entirely, or "topic exists but no data". See troubleshooting.md.

  1. In the Conduit app:
  2. Tap Settings → Transport: DDS
  3. Domain ID: must match ROS_DOMAIN_ID
  4. Distribution: your host's ROS 2 release (Lyrical by default)
  5. Tap Discovery. On the DDS Discovery page:
    • Peers: add the ROS 2 host's IP address. Without peers, Conduit uses multicast discovery only. With peers, it uses unicast to the peers on top of multicast.
    • Network Interface: en0 (WiFi) on iPhone and iPad (the default).
    • This Device shows the iPhone's address. Add it as a peer on the ROS 2 host too, in CYCLONEDDS_URI (see Transports).

  6. Tap Done. Settings are saved as you change them; discovery changes apply the next time you tap Start.

  7. Enable sensors and tap Play

Important:

  • Domain ID must match between the app and ROS 2 system. Valid range: 0-232 (DDS RTPS limit).
  • On iPhone and iPad, keep the network interface on en0 (WiFi). "auto" can pick a cellular or VPN interface.
  • Many Wi-Fi networks drop multicast. If discovery fails, add peers on both sides.

docs.title: Which ROS 2 versions are supported?
docs.text:
Conduit supports:

  • ROS 2 Humble (Ubuntu 22.04) - No type hash
  • ROS 2 Jazzy (Ubuntu 24.04) - RIHS01 type hash
  • ROS 2 Kilted (Ubuntu 24.04) - RIHS01 type hash
  • ROS 2 Lyrical (Ubuntu 26.04) - RIHS01 type hash
  • ROS 2 Rolling - RIHS01 type hash

Supported RMW implementations:

  • rmw_zenoh_cpp — via the Zenoh transport
  • rmw_cyclonedds_cpp — via the DDS transport. Use the version that ships with your distro. Conduit embeds CycloneDDS 11.0.1.

Set Settings → Distribution to match the host for either transport.

The default RMW on every one of these distros is Fast DDS (rmw_fastrtps_cpp), so set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION explicitly. A Fast DDS host can discover Conduit over DDS, but may drop or delay high-rate topics such as the camera and LiDAR.

docs.title: Why can't I see my topics in ros2 topic list?
docs.text:
Check these common issues:

  1. Domain IDs don't match (most common): 
    # Check domain ID on ROS 2 system
echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID
  2. Domain ID in app Settings must match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on host
  3. Default is 0 if not set

  4. Valid range: 0-232 (RTPS specification limit)

  5. Zenoh router not running: 

    # Start router with matching domain ID
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd

  6. Wrong RMW implementation: 

    # Verify RMW setting
echo $RMW_IMPLEMENTATION
# Zenoh transport: rmw_zenoh_cpp
# DDS transport:   rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
    After changing it, run ros2 daemon stop so the CLI picks up the new value.

  7. Network connectivity: Ensure iPhone and ROS 2 system are on the same network

  8. Firewall on the ROS 2 system: allow TCP 7447 for Zenoh, or the DDS UDP ports (7400 + 250 × domain and up) for DDS.

  9. Distribution mismatch: Settings → Distribution must match the host (Humble vs Jazzy and later).

The QR code script checks most of these on the host for you.

docs.title: What does the Distribution setting change?
docs.text:
• Humble: key expressions carry TypeHashNotSupported instead of a type hash.
  • Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical, Rolling: key expressions carry the RIHS01 type hash. These four share one wire format, so any of them works with any of these hosts.

Pick the release your host runs; there is no automatic detection.

docs.title: Can I use Conduit without a ROS 2 system?
docs.text:
Yes. Record mode works with no network at all. Choose Record next to the play button and Conduit writes the sensors to an .mcap file on the device. See MCAP recording.

To receive live data, you need a ROS 2 system (Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical, or Rolling) with one of the supported transports:

  • Zenoh: rmw_zenoh_cpp middleware and a running Zenoh router (rmw_zenohd).
  • DDS: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp middleware on the same LAN as your iPhone or iPad — no router required.

docs.title: Which sensors work on which platforms?
docs.text:
• iPhone: all 13 sensors. LiDAR needs a Pro model from iPhone 12 Pro on.
  • iPad: every sensor except Proximity. LiDAR needs an iPad Pro (2020 or later).
  • Mac (Mac Catalyst): Camera, Microphone, Battery, Thermal and Game Controller only.

Device Pose (Conduit 3) runs on iPhone and iPad only, and only while ARKit tracking is normal.

See Platform notes for details per platform, and Sensors and topics for every topic, message type, rate and frame.

docs.title: How do I enable background mode?
docs.text:
Turn on Settings → Publishing → Background Publishing. It needs the Background Mode In-App Purchase; until you buy it, the toggle shows a lock.

What happens when you leave the app:

  • Background Publishing off: Conduit stops publishing.
  • Background Publishing on: Camera and LiDAR stop (iOS does not allow them in the background). The other sensors keep publishing until iOS suspends the app, which it can do at any time.

Keep Conduit in the foreground when you need data for a long time, for example a long GPS track. See Known issues.

docs.text:

One-time In-App Purchases:

  • LiDAR — point cloud and depth (iPhone Pro / iPad Pro)

docs.title: How do I verify data is being published?
docs.text:
On your ROS 2 system:

# Check if topic appears
ros2 topic list | grep conduit

# Echo data from IMU sensor
ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu

# Check publish rate
ros2 topic hz /conduit/imu

# View topic info
ros2 topic info /conduit/imu --verbose

docs.title: Why does a sensor say "Waiting for subscriber"?
docs.text:
Requires Conduit 2.4.0 or later.

Publish only when subscribed (Settings → Publishing) is on, and none of that sensor's topics has a ROS 2 subscriber. The sensor is still running; Conduit just sends nothing until a subscriber appears. The row shows its normal rate again as soon as one connects. See On-demand capture for how the setting works.

If you expected data, check:

  1. Is anything subscribed? For example, run ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu on the host.
  2. Subscriber QoS. Sensor topics default to best effort. On DDS, a subscriber that requests reliable delivery does not match them. Subscribe with --qos-reliability best_effort (or qos_profile_sensor_data in rclpy), or set the sensor's QoS to Reliable in its settings.
  3. Domain ID and Distribution. ROS_DOMAIN_ID on the host must match the Domain ID in Conduit, and Settings → Distribution must match your host (Humble vs Jazzy and later).
  4. Want continuous publishing? Turn off Settings → Publishing → Publish only when subscribed. It is off by default.

docs.title: Why is my sensor showing "Not Available"?
docs.text:
Common reasons:

  1. Hardware limitation: Device doesn't have that sensor
  2. LiDAR: iPhone 12 Pro or later Pro models, iPad Pro (2020 or later)

  3. Proximity: iPhone only (not iPad)

  4. Platform limitation:

  5. Mac: only Camera, Microphone, Battery, Thermal and Game Controller. See Which sensors work on which platforms?

  6. Permission denied: Grant permission in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security

  7. Runtime unavailable:

  8. Game Controller: No controller connected
  9. Location: Location services disabled

docs.title: Can I use multiple cameras simultaneously?
docs.text:
Yes. Each camera has its own row:

  1. Turn on the cameras you want (front, wide, ultra-wide, telephoto)
  2. Each camera publishes to its own topics (default namespace conduit):
  3. /conduit/camera/front/image_raw/compressed
  4. /conduit/camera/wide/image_raw/compressed
  5. /conduit/camera/ultrawide/image_raw/compressed
  6. /conduit/camera/telephoto/image_raw/compressed

These are the default compressed outputs. With the camera's output set to raw, the image goes to .../image_raw instead. Each camera also publishes /conduit/camera/<camera>/camera_info.

Notes:

  • The wide, ultra-wide and telephoto cameras need the Back Cameras purchase. The front camera is free.
  • LiDAR uses ARKit, which gives only the wide camera. While LiDAR is on, only the wide camera streams; turning on another camera turns LiDAR off. LiDAR can also publish /conduit/camera/wide/depth/image_raw, aligned with the wide camera.

docs.title: How do I change the publishing rate?
docs.text:
1. Stop publishing. The settings button appears under each sensor's toggle.
  2. Tap the settings button (sliders icon) under the sensor's toggle
  3. Pick a rate from Rate (Hz)
  4. Change the QoS settings if needed
  5. Tap Save

Each sensor has its own maximum rate, shown in the sheet. See Sensors and topics for the default and maximum rates.

docs.title: What ROS 2 message type does the Microphone sensor use?
docs.text:
The Microphone sensor publishes audio_common_msgs/msg/AudioData messages.

Audio parameters:

  • Sample rate: 16,000 Hz
  • Channels: 1 (mono)
  • Format: S16LE (signed 16-bit little-endian PCM)
  • Samples per message: 1024
  • Publish rate: ~15.6 messages/sec

Default topic: /conduit/audio (configurable via namespace in Settings)

docs.title: How do I receive Microphone data on ROS 2?
docs.text:
You need the audio_common_msgs package installed on your ROS 2 system.

Using Docker (easiest): 

# The pre-built Docker image already includes audio_common_msgs
docker run -d -p 7447:7447 --name ros_lyrical_zenoh ghcr.io/youtalk/conduit-support:lyrical

# Echo audio messages
docker exec ros_lyrical_zenoh bash -c \
  "source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash && \
   source /ros2_ws/install/setup.bash && \
   export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp && \
   ros2 topic echo /conduit/audio audio_common_msgs/msg/AudioData"

Using a native ROS 2 installation: 

# Install audio_common (includes audio_common_msgs)
sudo apt install ros-lyrical-audio-common  # Lyrical
sudo apt install ros-jazzy-audio-common   # Jazzy
sudo apt install ros-humble-audio-common  # Humble

# Or build from source
mkdir -p ~/ros2_ws/src && cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone --branch ros2 --depth 1 https://github.com/ros-drivers/audio_common.git
cd ~/ros2_ws
rosdep install --from-paths src --ignore-src -r -y
colcon build --packages-select audio_common_msgs
source install/setup.bash

Verify the topic: 

# Check topic exists
ros2 topic list | grep audio

# Echo messages
ros2 topic echo /conduit/audio audio_common_msgs/msg/AudioData

# Check publish rate (~15-16 Hz)
ros2 topic hz /conduit/audio

# Inspect message type
ros2 topic info /conduit/audio --verbose

docs.title: How do I play back the audio data in Python?
docs.text:
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from audio_common_msgs.msg import AudioData
import numpy as np
import sounddevice as sd

class AudioPlayer(Node):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__('audio_player')
        self.subscription = self.create_subscription(
            AudioData,
            '/conduit/audio',
            self.audio_callback,
            10)
        self.sample_rate = 16000

    def audio_callback(self, msg):
        # Convert bytes to int16 numpy array
        samples = np.frombuffer(bytes(msg.data), dtype=np.int16)
        # Normalize to float32 [-1.0, 1.0]
        audio = samples.astype(np.float32) / 32768.0
        # Play audio (non-blocking)
        sd.play(audio, self.sample_rate)

def main():
    rclpy.init()
    player = AudioPlayer()
    rclpy.spin(player)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

docs.title: Does the Microphone sensor work in the background?
docs.text:
No. In the current release the microphone stops when Conduit goes to the background, even with Background Publishing on.

Keep the app in the foreground when using the Microphone sensor.

docs.title: How does MCAP recording work?
docs.text:
Choose Record or Both next to the play button, then tap play. Conduit writes every topic it produces to an .mcap file on the device, as the same XCDR v1 bytes it sends to ROS 2. The schemas are embedded in the file, so any MCAP reader (Foxglove, Lichtblick, ros2 bag play, the mcap CLI) opens it without external .msg files.

  • Publish: live to ROS 2 only.
  • Record: to a file only. Needs no network and no ROS 2 system.
  • Both: live to ROS 2 and to a file.

Recording is free. Recordings stay on the device; Conduit never uploads them. Open them from the folder button next to Settings in the toolbar, where you can delete them. To export a recording through the share sheet (Files, AirDrop, mail, …), you need the Recording Export purchase. Without it, recordings are kept in the app's private storage and the share button shows a lock.

docs.title: Can I record while publishing live to ROS 2?
docs.text: Yes. Choose Both. Recording is a sink on the same publish path, not a separate pipeline — every message you send to ROS 2 is also written to the file.

docs.title: How do I replay an MCAP file?
docs.text:
# Foxglove Studio: File → Open → select the .mcap

# ros2 bag (Jazzy / Kilted / Lyrical / Rolling — bundled mcap_storage_plugin):
ros2 bag play recording.mcap

# Humble: install ros-humble-rosbag2-storage-mcap first
sudo apt install ros-humble-rosbag2-storage-mcap
ros2 bag play recording.mcap --storage mcap

docs.title: Do I need a purchase to record?
docs.text: No. Recording to the device is free, and the Record and Both modes are always available. Only exporting a recording out of the app needs the one-time Recording Export purchase (see premium features).

docs.title: Does Conduit work offline?
docs.text:
Partly:

  • Record mode works with no network at all.
  • Publish and Both need a local network between your iPhone or iPad and the ROS 2 system (or a Zenoh router you can reach).

No internet is required for either.

docs.title: How do I reset app settings?
docs.text:
Delete and reinstall the app. This clears:

  • Connection settings (router address, peers, Domain ID, Distribution)
  • Sensor configurations
  • Recordings stored on the device

Purchases are tied to your Apple ID. After reinstalling, tap Settings → Premium Features → Restore Purchases.

To see the setup tour again without resetting anything, tap Settings → About & Help → Replay Onboarding.

docs.title: Is my data sent to the cloud?
docs.text:
No. All sensor data:

  • Stays on your local network (or your Tailscale tailnet, if you use one)
  • Goes only to the ROS 2 host or Zenoh router you configure
  • Is never uploaded to external servers
  • Is never shared with third parties

Firebase Analytics collects anonymous app usage statistics only, with no sensor values. To turn it off, open Settings → About & Help → Privacy and turn off Send Usage Statistics.

See our Privacy Policy for details.

docs.title: Known issues & limitations
docs.text: Current limitations and known issues in Conduit.

docs.title: Background GPS tracking not supported
docs.text:
Status: Limitation of the current release

Reason: Conduit does not ask for "Always" location permission, and iOS can suspend an app in the background at any time.

Current behavior:

  • GPS publishes while Conduit is in the foreground
  • With Settings → Publishing → Background Publishing off, GPS stops when you leave the app
  • With Background Publishing on, GPS may keep publishing for a while, but iOS can suspend Conduit at any time, so do not rely on it for a long track

Workaround:

  • Keep the app in the foreground during GPS data collection

docs.title: macOS: No IMU/GPS sensors
docs.text:
Status: Hardware limitation

Reason: Macs have no accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, barometer, ambient light sensor, GPS, proximity sensor or LiDAR that Conduit can read.

Available on Mac (Mac Catalyst): Camera, Microphone, Battery, Thermal and Game Controller. IMU, Magnetometer, Barometer, Illuminance, GPS, Proximity, LiDAR and Device Pose are not available.

Use case: Mac camera, microphone and game controller input, and development/testing. See Platform notes.

docs.title: Camera/LiDAR stop in background
docs.text:
Status: iOS system restriction

Reason: iOS doesn't allow camera/ARKit usage in background. Camera and LiDAR stop even with Background Publishing on. The Microphone also stops in the background in the current release.

Workaround: Keep app in foreground when using Camera, LiDAR or Microphone

docs.title: Proximity sensor only on iPhone
docs.text:
Status: Hardware limitation

Reason: iPads don't have proximity sensors.

Workaround: Use iPhone for proximity sensing, or use LiDAR for distance measurement

docs.title: Multiple cameras may cause memory warnings
docs.text:
Status: Known issue

Behavior: Enabling 3-4 cameras simultaneously may trigger iOS memory warnings.

Mitigation:

  • On a memory warning, Conduit stops all cameras and LiDAR
  • Reduce number of active cameras
  • Lower the camera's Resolution in its settings

Workaround: Enable only cameras you need

docs.title: High frame rate may cause thermal throttling
docs.text:
Status: Expected behavior

Reason: Continuous 100 Hz IMU + multi-camera can heat device.

Mitigation:

  • iOS will throttle CPU/GPU when too hot
  • Rates may automatically decrease

Workaround:

  • Reduce publishing rates
  • Disable unused sensors
  • Allow device to cool between sessions

docs.title: Initial connection can be slow
docs.text:
Status: Normal behavior

Reason: Opening the Zenoh session or DDS participant and creating a publisher for each sensor can take a few seconds. Conduit retries each initial connect up to 3 times before it reports "Connection Failed".

Workaround: Wait for "Publishing" state before expecting data

docs.title: Connection lost not always detected immediately
docs.text:
Status: Known limitation

Reason: A router or host that goes away is noticed only when a send fails.

Behavior: Data can stop for a while before Conduit notices. Once a send fails, Conduit reconnects in the background: it retries after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds, then every 30 seconds, with no limit. If the device loses its network entirely, Conduit stops publishing and shows Connection Lost.

Workaround: Wait for the next retry, or stop and start publishing. See Connection drops and reconnects.

docs.title: rmw_zenoh_cpp version sensitivity
docs.text:
Status: By design

Reason: Wire format changes between rmw_zenoh_cpp versions.

Mitigation:

  • Settings → Distribution: Humble, or Jazzy / Kilted / Lyrical / Rolling (one shared wire format)

Known compatible versions:

  • ROS 2 Humble: rmw_zenoh_cpp (Humble release)
  • ROS 2 Jazzy: rmw_zenoh_cpp (Jazzy release)
  • ROS 2 Kilted: rmw_zenoh_cpp (Kilted release)
  • ROS 2 Lyrical: rmw_zenoh_cpp (Lyrical release)
  • ROS 2 Rolling: rmw_zenoh_cpp (Rolling)

Workaround: Set Distribution to match the host.

docs.title: Camera/LiDAR fragmentation loss on DDS over WiFi
docs.text:
Status: Known limitation

Reason: Large RTPS messages (>1400 bytes — camera, LiDAR, CameraInfo with large K matrices) are split into UDP fragments. Consumer WiFi often drops or reorders fragments, especially over multicast.

Mitigation:

  • Add peers in Settings → Discovery → Peers, and add the iPhone's address as a peer on the host. With peers, Conduit sends over unicast on top of multicast.
  • Reduce camera resolution, or turn on LiDAR point cloud compression.
  • Use wired Ethernet on the ROS 2 host if possible.

docs.title: CameraInfo requires BestEffort subscriber QoS
docs.text:
Status: By design

Reason: CameraInfo publishes with BestEffort + TransientLocal QoS (latchedBestEffort) to match DDS behavior on iOS. Standard image_transport subscribers default to Reliable, which does not match.

Workaround: Override the subscriber QoS: 

ros2 topic echo /conduit/camera/front/camera_info \
  --qos-reliability best_effort \
  --qos-durability transient_local

docs.title: Disconnect delay on DDS
docs.text:
Status: Expected behavior

Reason: Closing the DDS publishers and the DDS participant takes some time.

Behavior: After you press Stop, it can take a few seconds before the app fully releases the domain. No action is needed.

docs.title: DDS requires WiFi — no cellular fallback
docs.text:
Status: By design

Reason: DDS discovery binds to a specific network interface (en0 on iOS). Cellular or VPN interfaces are not supported; multicast/unicast discovery requires the device and the ROS 2 host to be on the same LAN.

Workaround: Use the Zenoh transport if you need to cross networks, for example over Tailscale (see Connect with a QR code) or with a router address you can reach.

docs.title: Premium purchase required for some sensors
docs.text:
Status: By design (business model)

Free:

  • IMU, GPS, Magnetometer, Barometer, Illuminance, Proximity, Battery, Thermal, Microphone
  • Front camera
  • MCAP recording to the device

One-time In-App Purchases:

  • Back Cameras — Wide, Ultra Wide and Telephoto cameras in one purchase
  • LiDAR
  • Game Controller
  • Background Mode — keep publishing while the app is in the background
  • Recording Export — export and share recorded .mcap files

docs.title: Premium purchases not syncing
docs.text:
Status: Rare issue

Reason: App Store receipt verification delay.

Solutions:

  1. Restart app
  2. Restore purchases (Settings → Premium Features → Restore Purchases)
  3. Verify Apple ID is correct

docs.title: Workaround summary
docs.text: Issue Workaround Background GPS Keep app in foreground macOS no IMU / GPS Use iPhone/iPad Camera background Keep app in foreground Memory warnings Reduce active sensors Thermal throttling Lower rates, fewer sensors Connection slow Wait for "Publishing" Connection drops Wait for the automatic reconnect DDS fragmentation loss on WiFi Add discovery peers on both sides; lower camera resolution or compress LiDAR CameraInfo QoS mismatch Subscriber: --qos-reliability best_effort --qos-durability transient_local DDS disconnect delay Expected behavior — no user action required DDS over WAN / cellular Use Zenoh transport with a public router instead

docs.title: Reporting new issues
docs.text:
Found a bug not listed here? Create an issue with:

  • Platform and OS version
  • Sensor type affected
  • Steps to reproduce
  • Expected vs actual behavior

docs.title: Feature requests
docs.text:
Want a new feature? Request it here

We prioritize based on:

  • User impact
  • Technical feasibility
  • Platform constraints
  • Development resources

docs.title: On-demand capture
docs.text: Conduit 2.4.0 adds Publish only when subscribed. The sensors keep running, but a topic sends data only while a ROS 2 subscriber is connected to it. Use it to pull a single camera frame, point cloud, or sensor reading when you ask for it, instead of streaming every topic all the time.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
1. Open Settings (gear icon) in Conduit.
  2. Under Publishing, turn on Publish only when subscribed.

Good to know:

  • It is off by default, so existing setups keep publishing continuously.
  • It is one app-wide setting. It applies to every sensor topic; there is no per-sensor switch. Latched topics such as /tf_static always publish (see below).
  • It works with both the Zenoh and DDS transports.

docs.title: What you will see
docs.text:
• A sensor row shows Waiting for subscriber in place of its rate when none of that sensor's topics has a subscriber. The sensor itself is still running. Camera and LiDAR publish more than one topic, so their rows keep showing the rate while any one of their topics has a subscriber.
  • When a topic has no subscriber and one appears, Conduit starts sending it and drops anything captured before that moment, so a lone subscriber's first message is a fresh capture. If another subscriber is already connected to the topic, you join the stream that is already running. For camera and depth topics on Wi-Fi, the first message typically arrives within about 0.2 to 0.3 s. Low-rate sensors such as GPS, Battery and Thermal (1 Hz) can take up to one publish period.
  • When the last subscriber disconnects, the topic goes back to waiting.

docs.title: What is never held back
docs.text:
• Recording. Recording is never held back: it records the running sensors whether or not the setting is on and whether or not a subscriber is connected.
  • Latched topics such as /tf_static. They always publish, and subscribers that join late still receive them.

docs.title: Capture a single message
docs.text:
If nothing else is subscribed to the topic, the first message is captured after you subscribe, so ros2 topic echo --once takes a fresh picture:

ros2 topic echo --once /conduit/camera/wide/image_raw/compressed

The same from Python:

import rclpy
from rclpy.qos import qos_profile_sensor_data
from rclpy.wait_for_message import wait_for_message
from sensor_msgs.msg import CompressedImage

rclpy.init()
node = rclpy.create_node("conduit_capture")
ok, image = wait_for_message(
    CompressedImage,
    node,
    "/conduit/camera/wide/image_raw/compressed",
    qos_profile=qos_profile_sensor_data,
    time_to_wait=5.0,
)
if ok:
    print("captured at", image.header.stamp)
else:
    print("timed out: no message within 5 s")
node.destroy_node()
rclpy.shutdown()

The examples use the Camera sensor's default compressed output.

docs.title: Capture an RGB and depth pair
docs.text:
For a color image and a depth image of the same frame (LiDAR mode; needs an iPhone 12 Pro or newer, or an iPad Pro from 2020 or newer):

  1. Enable the Camera sensor with the Wide camera, and the LiDAR sensor. The Wide camera and LiDAR are premium features (one-time In-App Purchases).
  2. Open the LiDAR sensor's settings and set Output to Depth or Both. The default, Point Cloud, publishes no depth image.
  3. Subscribe to both topics, for example /conduit/camera/wide/image_raw/compressed and /conduit/camera/wide/depth/image_raw.
  4. Take one message from each and match them by equal header.stamp.

Each topic starts sending when its own subscriber appears, so only frames captured after both subscribers are connected form a pair.

docs.title: Subscriber QoS
docs.text:
Sensor topics publish with best effort reliability by default. On DDS, a subscriber that asks for reliable delivery does not match them, so it receives nothing and the sensor keeps showing Waiting for subscriber. Either:

  • subscribe with best effort (qos_profile_sensor_data in rclpy, --qos-reliability best_effort on the ros2 CLI), or
  • set the sensor's QoS to Reliable in its settings.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• If a subscriber disconnects and reconnects within about 50 ms, Conduit may not notice the gap, so its first message can be slightly older than the new subscription (but never older than the previous one).
  • Only messages that carry a header stamp are checked against the subscription time. For topics without one, such as the Microphone's audio, the first message is not guaranteed to be newer than the subscription.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: If a sensor says Waiting for subscriber and you expected data, see Why does a sensor say "Waiting for subscriber"? in the FAQ. To go back to continuous publishing, turn off Publish only when subscribed in Settings → Publishing.

docs.title: Connect with a QR code
docs.text:
Open in Conduit

Conduit is installed but didn't open? Tap the button.

Conduit not installed? Install Conduit 2.6.0 or later from the App Store, then scan the QR code again. The script on your PC keeps waiting.

A script on your ROS 2 PC checks the setup, shows a QR code, and waits for Conduit to check in. Scan the code with the iPhone's Camera app and Conduit fills in the connection settings for you.

Needs Conduit 2.6.0 or later

QR pairing arrives in Conduit 2.6.0. Settings → About & Help shows your version. With an older version, set up the connection by hand: see Zenoh or DDS.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A native PC (not WSL, not inside a container) running Ubuntu, RHEL or Fedora, with ROS 2 sourced in the shell you run the script from:

    System ROS 2 Ubuntu Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical, Rolling RHEL 8 Humble RHEL 9 Jazzy, Kilted RHEL 10 Lyrical Fedora Lyrical

    RHEL rebuilds such as Rocky Linux and AlmaLinux count as RHEL. Install ROS 2 with the official instructions. Windows is not supported yet.

  • RMW_IMPLEMENTATION set to rmw_zenoh_cpp or rmw_cyclonedds_cpp. Fast DDS (the default when it is unset) works, but may drop or delay high-rate topics such as the camera and LiDAR.

  • The iPhone and the PC on the same Wi-Fi, or on the same Tailscale tailnet.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://conduit.direct/pair.sh | bash

Options go after bash -s --, for example curl -fsSL https://conduit.direct/pair.sh | bash -s -- --tailscale. Run bash -s -- --help to list them.

docs.title: Read it first
docs.text:
The script is a single file. To read it before running it:

curl -fsSL https://conduit.direct/pair.sh | less

It installs nothing and never uses sudo. It asks before it changes anything outside its own run (for example before adding the iPhone to ~/.bashrc), and it leaves no process running when it exits.

docs.title: What it asks
docs.text:
• Whether to continue with Fast DDS, if that is your RMW (CycloneDDS is recommended).
  • Whether to add the iPhone as a discovery peer on this PC (DDS), and whether to add the matching line to ~/.bashrc. The default answer to both is no.

For Zenoh, if the router is not running, the script offers to start it in the background. The router keeps running after the script ends; the script prints its log file and the kill command that stops it. Answer no to start it yourself (ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd); the script then waits for it.

docs.title: Tailscale
docs.text: To pair over the internet or across subnets, put the iPhone and the PC on one tailnet and run the script with --tailscale. Tailscale works with Zenoh only, so set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp first.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
If nothing happens after you scan the QR code, the script prints what to check. In short:

Conduit never checks in

  • If the firewall (ufw on Ubuntu, firewalld on RHEL and Fedora) is on, allow the check-in port (7449 by default, TCP) and Conduit's ports: TCP 7447 for Zenoh, or UDP 7400 + 250 x domain through the next 249 ports for DDS. The script prints the exact commands when the iPhone does not show up.
  • The iPhone must be on the same Wi-Fi as the PC. Guest and office Wi-Fi often isolate clients from each other; try another network or a hotspot.
  • Allow Local Network access for Conduit: iPhone Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network.
  • With Tailscale, open the Tailscale app on the iPhone and connect it to the same tailnet as the PC.
  • Scan the QR code again if Conduit did not open from it.

Conduit checked in but did not appear in the ROS 2 graph

  • Did you tap Start in Conduit?
  • For Zenoh, the router must keep running.
  • If the iPhone's address changed, run the script again.

Conduit is in the graph but no message arrived on /tf_static

  • For DDS, shells that run ROS 2 nodes need the export line the script prints (or a new shell after adding it to ~/.bashrc). Restart ROS 2 nodes that were already running and run ros2 daemon stop.
  • With Fast DDS, switch to CycloneDDS: export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp.
  • If the iPhone's address changed, run the script again.

See also Zenoh or DDS and Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Platform notes
docs.text: Conduit runs on iPhone and iPad (iOS and iPadOS 16 or later) and on Mac (macOS 13 or later, as a Mac Catalyst app). The sensors you can use depend on the device. For every topic, message type and rate, see Sensors and topics.

docs.title: Sensors by platform
docs.text:
Sensor iPhone iPad Mac IMU ✅ ✅ ❌ Magnetic Field ✅ ✅ ❌ Barometer ✅ ✅ ❌ Illuminance ✅ ✅ ❌ GPS ✅ ✅ ❌ Proximity ✅ ❌ ❌ Device Pose (Conduit 3) ✅ ✅ ❌ Camera ✅ ✅ ✅ built-in camera only LiDAR ✅ iPhone 12 Pro and later Pro models ✅ iPad Pro (2020 and later) ❌ Microphone ✅ ✅ ✅ Battery ✅ ✅ ✅ Thermal ✅ ✅ ✅ Game Controller ✅ ✅ ✅

A sensor the device does not have shows as Not Available. Tap it to see the reason.

docs.title: iPhone
docs.text:
iPhone has all 13 sensors.

  • LiDAR needs an iPhone 12 Pro or a later Pro model.
  • Cameras: the front camera and the back cameras your model has (Wide, Ultra Wide, Telephoto). While LiDAR is on, only the Wide camera streams, because ARKit provides only that camera.
  • Illuminance is estimated from the camera's exposure, so it cannot run together with a camera stream, LiDAR or Device Pose.
  • Device Pose (Conduit 3) uses ARKit world tracking and publishes only while tracking is normal.

docs.title: iPad
docs.text:
iPad has every sensor except Proximity.

  • LiDAR needs an iPad Pro (2020 or later).
  • GPS: iPad models without cellular have no GPS receiver. Location then comes from Wi-Fi and is less accurate.
  • Cameras: an iPad with Center Stage shows its front camera once, as the front camera.

docs.title: Mac (Mac Catalyst)
docs.text:
On a Mac, Conduit can use:

  • Camera: the built-in FaceTime HD camera. External cameras and Continuity Camera are not listed.
  • Microphone
  • Battery: on a Mac with a battery.
  • Thermal
  • Game Controller

Macs have no motion sensors, GPS, barometer or LiDAR, so those sensors show as Not Available.

In Robots (Conduit 3), the robot arm view only watches on a Mac; moving the arm needs an iPhone or iPad.

docs.title: Background publishing
docs.text:
Settings → Publishing → Background Publishing keeps sensors publishing after you leave the app. It needs the Background Mode In-App Purchase.

  • Camera and LiDAR stop in the background (iOS restriction).
  • The other sensors keep publishing until iOS suspends the app, which it can do at any time.

Keep Conduit in the foreground when you need data for a long time. See Known issues.

docs.title: Network
docs.text:
• Zenoh works over any network that can reach the router over TCP, including a Tailscale tailnet.
  • DDS needs the device and the ROS 2 host on the same LAN. On iPhone and iPad, select en0 (WiFi) as the network interface (Settings → Discovery).

See Transports.

docs.title: Privacy Policy
docs.text:
Last Updated: November 5, 2026

Conduit is a developer tool that publishes sensor data from iPhone, iPad and Mac to ROS 2 (Robot Operating System 2) networks. It is built on the open-source swift-ros2 library, which speaks the ROS 2 wire formats directly over Zenoh or DDS. There is no Conduit-operated server in between. This policy explains what data the app uses, where it goes, and your choices.

Developer: Yutaka Kondo (youtalk) · LinkedIn · Website

docs.title: Sensor data
docs.text:
Conduit reads a sensor only after you turn that sensor on. All sensors are off by default. Depending on what you turn on, this can include:

  • Motion: accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer (IMU, Magnetic Field)
  • Location: GPS position
  • Camera: images from the device cameras
  • Depth and pose: LiDAR depth and the device's position and orientation from ARKit (on supported devices)
  • Audio: microphone samples
  • Environment: air pressure (Barometer) and a brightness estimate from the camera (Illuminance)
  • Proximity: the near/far reading of the proximity sensor
  • Device state: battery level and thermal state
  • Game controller input: buttons and sticks of a connected controller

Where it goes:

  • Live publishing: Conduit sends sensor data only to the Zenoh router or DDS peers you configure, usually on your own network. It is not sent to us or to any third party.
  • Recordings: when you record, Conduit writes the same sensor messages to an .mcap file on the device. Recordings stay on the device unless you share them (for example through the share sheet, Files or AirDrop). Conduit never uploads them.
  • Location access is "While Using the App" only. Conduit reads your location only while the GPS sensor is on.

docs.title: Connecting with a QR code
docs.text:
When you scan a pairing QR code from the Conduit pairing script (Connect with a QR code):

  • The connection settings are in the part of the link after #. If the link opens in a browser, the browser does not send that part to the web server; the page only passes it to Conduit.

  • After Conduit applies the settings, it sends one line of JSON over TCP to the pairing script on your computer, at the address in the QR code. The line contains:

    • the one-time token from the QR code,
    • the device's name (as set in iOS or iPadOS Settings),
    • the Conduit version,
    • the ROS 2 node name and namespace set in Conduit.

  • The script uses this to confirm that the device checked in. Nothing is sent anywhere else.

docs.title: Usage statistics
docs.text:
Conduit uses Firebase Analytics (Google) to collect anonymous usage statistics:

  • Device information: device model, OS version
  • App usage: for example which sensors are turned on or off, connection starts, stops and errors, and settings changes
  • Anonymous identifiers: an app instance identifier generated by Firebase

Conduit does not send sensor values, recordings, or the addresses and names you enter in Settings. Firebase may derive a coarse location, such as the country, from the network connection. We use these statistics only to find bugs and improve the app. They are processed by Google under the Firebase privacy information and Google's Privacy Policy.

To turn them off, open Settings in Conduit → About & Help → Privacy and turn off Send Usage Statistics.

docs.title: Data stored on the device
docs.text:
• Settings (connection, sensors, rates and so on) are stored on the device.
  • Recordings stay on the device until you delete them in Conduit or in Files, or delete the app.
  • Earlier versions of Conduit stored a random 16-byte ROS 2 publisher ID in the Keychain. Current versions do not use it.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Permission Purpose Required Local Network Connect to the Zenoh router or DDS peers on your network, and to the pairing script Yes, to publish Camera Camera images; also used by LiDAR, Device Pose and Illuminance Optional Microphone Audio samples Optional Location (While Using the App) GPS position Optional Motion & Fitness IMU and magnetometer Optional

Conduit asks for a permission when you first turn on a sensor that needs it. You can change permissions at any time in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security.

docs.title: In-App Purchases
docs.text: Some features are one-time In-App Purchases through Apple's App Store: Back Cameras (Wide, Ultra Wide and Telephoto; the front camera is free), LiDAR, Game Controller, Background Mode and Recording Export. Apple handles payment, receipts and refunds. Conduit only learns which features you have unlocked; it does not see or store payment information. See Apple's App Store & Privacy page.

docs.title: Your choices
docs.text:
• Sensors: turn any sensor on or off at any time.
  • Usage statistics: turn off Send Usage Statistics in Conduit's Settings → About & Help.
  • Recordings: delete them in Conduit at any time.
  • All app data: delete the app to remove its settings and recordings.

docs.title: Data retention
docs.text:
• Live sensor data: not kept by the app; it is sent as it is captured.
  • Recordings: kept on the device until you delete them or delete the app.
  • Settings: kept until you delete the app.
  • Usage statistics: kept by Firebase under its retention policy.

docs.title: Policy updates
docs.text: We may update this policy. Changes are posted on this page with a new "Last Updated" date.

docs.title: Contact
docs.text:
• LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/youtalk
  • Website: https://youtalk.jp

Note: Conduit is designed for developers and researchers. It is not intended for children under 13.

docs.title: Recording (MCAP)
docs.text: Conduit can write every topic it publishes to an MCAP file on the device. Open the file in Foxglove or Lichtblick, or replay it into a ROS 2 graph with ros2 bag play. Recording is free.

docs.title: Record
docs.text:
Next to the Start button, pick what Start does:

Mode What happens Publish Sends the topics to ROS 2. Nothing is recorded Record Writes the topics to an MCAP file. No network or ROS 2 host is needed Both Sends the topics to ROS 2 and records them

Turn on the sensors you want, then tap Start. Tap it again to stop and close the file.

A recording holds the same messages, with the same stamps, as the live topics, plus /tf_static, so viewers can place point clouds and camera images in 3D. Each file carries the message definitions it uses, so it opens without your .msg files.

docs.title: Find your recordings
docs.text:
Tap the folder button next to Settings. The list shows each recording's file name, size and date, and the total size at the top. Swipe a recording to delete it.

Files are named conduit_<yyyy-MM-dd>_<HH-mm-ss>.mcap, in the device's local time.

docs.title: Share a recording
docs.text:
Sharing a recording off the device needs the Recording Export purchase (Settings → Premium Features). With it:

  • The share button on a recording opens the share sheet: AirDrop, Files, Mail and so on.
  • Recordings are kept in Documents/Recordings, which the Files app (iPhone and iPad) and Finder (Mac, with the iPhone connected) can open. Recordings made before the purchase move there too.

Without it, recordings stay in Conduit's private storage and the share button shows a lock.

docs.title: Open a recording
docs.text:
Foxglove or Lichtblick: open the .mcap file. The file is indexed, so the timeline and seeking work right away.

ros2 bag: Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical and Rolling read MCAP out of the box. Humble needs the MCAP storage plugin first.

# Humble only
sudo apt install ros-humble-rosbag2-storage-mcap

ros2 bag info conduit_2026-11-05_09-30-00.mcap
ros2 bag play conduit_2026-11-05_09-30-00.mcap

audio_common_msgs/AudioData and point_cloud_interfaces/CompressedPointCloud2 are not in a default ROS 2 install. To play those topics back into ROS 2, install the packages that define them (see the FAQ for audio_common_msgs), or choose the topics to play with ros2 bag play --topics.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Camera and LiDAR fill the device quickly. Lower the camera resolution or rate in the sensor's settings for long recordings.
  • In the background, camera and LiDAR stop (an iOS restriction), so they leave a gap in the recording.
  • See the FAQ for more.

docs.title: Teleoperate a robot arm
docs.text:
Coming in Conduit 3

Robots is part of Conduit 3, which is not on the App Store yet. The Conduit on the App Store today (2.x) publishes sensors but has no robot button. This page describes Robots as it will ship in Conduit 3.

While you hold HOLD, the arm's end effector follows the motion of your iPhone or iPad: Conduit turns ARKit's pose of the device into geometry_msgs/TwistStamped for MoveIt Servo (/servo_node/delta_twist_cmds by default). A gripper arc works the gripper, and a pose menu sends the arm to a named pose through MoveIt. On a Mac the arm view is view-only.

docs.title: Host setup
docs.text:
Arms need MoveIt Servo from Jazzy or later: the arm profile reads moveit_msgs/ServoStatus and the overlay uses the moveit_servo. parameter namespace, which Humble's Servo publishes and configures differently.

  1. Servo overlay. Load conduit_teleop's Servo overlay after your robot's own Servo parameters, so Servo takes speeds and keeps twists for 0.5 s. The Servo overlay section below shows the file and how to load it.

  2. Time sync. Servo drops a twist whose stamp is older than incoming_command_timeout on its own clock, and it keeps moving on the last twist until then. Conduit therefore stamps every twist, moving or zero, on the robot's clock instead of the device's. It measures that clock from the profile's Joint states topic: the difference between each message's header.stamp and the time it arrives, taking the lowest-latency sample over the last 10 s, and it never stamps a twist ahead of the robot's real time. The 0.5 s stop when the link is lost then holds even when the device's clock differs from the host's, so neither chrony nor Set Automatically is needed for it. The requirements on the Joint states topic:

    • It must be stamped by the computer that runs Servo (the same clock Servo uses), and never in the future. Joint states published by another computer, such as a robot controller while Servo runs on a laptop, are measured as if they were Servo's clock, and Conduit cannot tell.
    • An empty Joint states field is saved as /joint_states. A namespaced topic, for example /arm/joint_states, must be in the field.
    • The host must run on wall-clock time. With simulation time (use_sim_time), HOLD cannot be used.

    HOLD is refused until the robot clock is known. The status line says why:

    Message Meaning "Reading the robot clock from Joint states" Conduit is still collecting stamps (it needs ten Joint states messages). "Robot and device clocks are more than a day apart (simulation time?). HOLD is off." The stamps are not wall-clock time: simulation time, unstamped messages, or a clock that was never set. "Set Joint states in the profile. HOLD needs the robot clock." The profile has no Joint states topic.

    If the robot clock becomes unusable while HOLD is held (a simulator starts, say), the arm lets go and shows "Robot clock changed. Release and press again."

  3. Gripper (optional). A control_msgs/action/GripperCommand server. The profile holds its action name (Gripper action) and, in its Gripper section, the open and closed positions in metres (Open (m), Closed (m); the Franka Panda's fingers travel from 0.0 to 0.04). With Gripper joint set to the finger joint in Joint states, the arm view shows the opening the robot reports.

  4. Named poses (optional). A move_group that publishes the SRDF on /robot_description_semantic and serves /move_action, and Servo's pause service. Conduit sends the moves itself, so there is nothing to install for them, and the profile needs nothing. See Named poses.

When the arm view opens, Conduit calls the profile's Servo command type service (/servo_node/switch_command_type by default) to switch Servo to TWIST, and retries every few seconds while Servo is missing or refuses. The Servo chip shows the result: "Connecting to Servo", "Servo not found", "Servo refused TWIST", then TWIST, or what Servo reports ("Slowing: near singularity", "Halted: joint bound", …), and "Servo not responding" when no Servo status has arrived for a second. HOLD stays off until Servo is ready.

docs.title: The arm view
docs.text:
The arm view runs the Device Pose sensor, which uses ARKit and needs the camera to itself, so opening it pauses the enabled sensors that use the camera (the cameras, except the wide back camera while LiDAR is on, whose images already come from ARKit) and Illuminance. When any of them is enabled, Conduit asks first ("Opening pauses … while the arm view is open. Device Pose uses ARKit, which needs the camera to itself. Continue?"). Closing the view restarts what it paused and stops Device Pose if the view started it.

The wrist camera fills the screen behind the controls. Pinch it to scale between the whole image and filling the screen, and drag to pan where the image is larger than the screen. Each layout keeps its own zoom.

On iPhone the layout follows how you hold the phone; with the rotation lock on, it stays as it is. Turning the phone releases HOLD and stops a gripper drag, and keeps the alignment. Closing the view returns the app to portrait.

  • Landscape, two hands. Along the top: the status chips and the status line, the pose menu and Align, then the gear and close. In the bottom corners, the gripper arc under one thumb and HOLD under the other. Without a Gripper action there is no arc, and HOLD sits in the bottom right corner. An iPad always uses this layout, in any orientation.
  • Upright, one hand. Along the top: the status chips, the gear and close; under them the pose menu and Align. The status line sits above the bottom controls. HOLD is in the bottom corner under the thumb of the hand that holds the phone, with the gripper arc around it.

The status chips: Servo, motion tracking (only while it is not normal, for example "tracking limited (excessive motion)" or "no tracking"), the wrist camera's latency and frame rate ("42 ms · 30 fps") and, when the profile has a Diagnostics topic, the diagnostics. Tap the diagnostics chip to open the diagnostics; this releases HOLD, stops a gripper drag and cancels a pose move. The status line appears only when something needs saying: a fault, a refusal, why HOLD is off, a pose move, or the free-time notice. The camera's captions (STALE, "No data", "No wrist camera topic", …) and the warning that the profile expects other connection settings sit in the space between the controls.

When the top row runs out of room (a smaller iPhone, larger text), the pose menu narrows (a long pose name is cut at its end) down to the width of "Poses", then shows only its symbol, and last Align shows only its symbol.

The gear's panel holds the settings that change the motion:

setting values what it does Max speed 0.5×, 1× (default), 2× Scales translation. At 1× the end effector moves at up to 0.25 m/s. Translation on (default) / off Off sends no translation, so the end effector turns without moving. Rotation on (default) / off Off sends no rotation. Rotation goes up to 1 rad/s. Gripper Left thumb (default) / Right thumb Landscape, with a Gripper action: which bottom corner has the gripper arc; HOLD takes the other. Hand Left hand / Right hand (default) Upright: the hand that holds the phone, which gets HOLD and the arc.

Gripper and Hand are one choice: the hand that holds the phone upright is the one whose thumb has HOLD in landscape. Conduit keeps it per robot on the device. Max speed, Translation and Rotation start at their defaults each time the view opens. The panel is off while HOLD is held.

docs.title: Using it
docs.text:
1. Align. Stand behind the robot's base and face the way its base frame's +x axis points, which is the robot's forward direction. Point the back camera that way, or tilt the device down to watch the screen, down to lying flat with the top of the screen pointing that way, and tap Align: that heading becomes the base frame's +x. If you face the robot instead, the motion is mirrored. Align says why when it refuses: "Tilt the device down: the camera points too far up" (the camera points more than 60° above the horizon), "Point the top of the screen toward the robot's front" or "Wait for motion tracking, then Align". Align again after motion tracking restarts or fails ("Motion tracking restarted. Align again.", "Motion tracking failed. Align again.").

  2. Hold HOLD and move. HOLD is dimmed until the link is up, Servo is ready, the robot clock is known and you have tapped Align. The status line says what it waits for ("Connecting…", a Servo problem, the robot clock, "Starting…"). A press when only Align is missing opens a "Tap Align first" dialog. A press also needs normal motion tracking, and is refused with "Waiting for motion tracking" or "Motion tracking is limited. Move the device slowly." without it. HOLD turns green and reads HOLDING while the arm follows.

  3. Release to stop. Releasing HOLD sends three zero twists at once. Tracking loss, a covered camera, a pose jump or a lost link also stop the arm, with one zero twist ("The pose jumped. Release and press again.", "Motion tracking paused. Release and press again."); release and press again to resume.

  4. Gripper. With HOLD released, tap the arc to open or close the gripper, or drag along it to set an opening. The readout along the arc says "40 % open" ("Moving · 40 % open" while a goal runs). The white handle is the opening asked for, and with a Gripper joint the track fills teal up to the opening the robot reports. Until the opening is known the readout says "Unknown: tap the arc": a drag sends nothing, and a tap opens. The gripper is off while HOLD is held ("Off while HOLD is held"), and a HOLD press while your thumb is on the gripper is refused with "Lift your thumb off the gripper first".

Without Conduit Plus, the status line shows the weekly free time's warnings for a few seconds ("30 minutes of free time left this week", "5 minutes left — the session stops when this week's free time is used up"). When the free time is used up while you hold HOLD or a pose move runs, the arm keeps going until you release HOLD and the move ends, for at most 5 more minutes. Then Conduit stops the arm and shows the Conduit Plus paywall over the arm view; closing the paywall closes the arm view.

VoiceOver: HOLD is the "Clutch" button: double-tap and hold to move the arm, and release to stop. The gripper is the adjustable "Gripper opening": double-tap to open or close it, swipe up or down to open or close it by 10 %, with Open and Close as actions. The wrist camera has "Show whole image" and "Fill screen" actions.

Conduit also publishes the raw pose (<namespace>/pose, /tf) and <namespace>/teleop/clutch (std_msgs/Bool, true while the clutch is held, false on any pose discontinuity), so a custom consumer can move relative to the pose at engage time. The namespace is conduit unless you changed it in Settings. The pose and /tf come from the Device Pose sensor, which runs while the arm view is open.

docs.title: Named poses
docs.text: The pose menu moves the arm to a group state of the robot's SRDF, such as stand or home, through MoveIt. Conduit talks to move_group itself: a pick sends a moveit_msgs/action/MoveGroup goal to /move_action, and Conduit pauses MoveIt Servo for the move. The host needs no extra node and nothing to install for poses, and the robot profile has no pose settings. Named poses work on Jazzy and later.

docs.title: The pose menu
docs.text:
The menu sits next to Align and lists every group state of the robot's arm group, in the order the SRDF has them and with the names exactly as the SRDF writes them (work, stand, ready, home, not "Work"). The pose the arm is at is checked.

  • The button reads the name of the pose the arm is at, or "Poses" when it is at none of them. At a pose it is teal with a checkmark. While the arm moves to a pose, it shows a spinner and the name of the pose you picked. A name longer than the button is cut at its end.
  • Picking a pose moves the arm there at once; there is no confirmation. Picking the pose the arm is already moving to does nothing. Picking another pose while the arm moves cancels that move and starts the new one once the cancel has ended.
  • The menu is off (the button is dimmed and does not open) while HOLD is pressed or held, while the link is down, after the session stopped or the view failed to set up, and for 1 s after the set of poses changes (the SRDF arrived late, or a changed SRDF dropped or reordered a pose). The pause keeps a tap meant for Align from moving the arm. VoiceOver says why: "Off while HOLD is held.", "Off while the robot link is down.", "Off: the session stopped.", "The pose list just changed.".
  • No menu appears without an SRDF that has states for the arm group. The menu appears as soon as the SRDF arrives. The Mac's view-only arm view has no menu.

The arm group is the parent_group of the SRDF's end effector. When several end effectors name a parent group, the first whose group has states counts. Without an end effector, it is the first group that is not an end effector's own group. The gripper's own states (such as open and closed) are therefore not offered. The goals plan for that group. A state name that an SRDF repeats is listed once and moves to the last state of that name, as in MoveIt; two names that differ only in case are two poses.

Conduit reads the SRDF from /robot_description_semantic and sends goals to /move_action, both absolute names. A move_group in a namespace publishes and serves them under that namespace, so the arm view finds no poses and shows no menu.

docs.title: What a pick does
docs.text:
• The goal plans and executes a move of the arm group to the state's joint positions, read from the newest SRDF when the move starts: one joint constraint per joint of the state, at ±0.001 rad, from the arm's current state, with one planning attempt, 5 s planning time, and velocity and acceleration scaled to 0.2.
  • Servo is paused before the goal and resumed when the move ends, whether it succeeds, fails or is cancelled. Conduit uses Servo's std_srvs/srv/SetBool pause service next to the profile's Servo command type service: /servo_node/pause_servo by default. While the move runs, the Servo chip reads "Servo paused for the pose move". Without the pause service, the move still runs. When the arm view connects, Conduit also resumes Servo, in case an earlier session left it paused.
  • The status line reads "Moving to stand…" while the move runs. The checkmark comes from the profile's Joint states topic: the arm is at a pose when every joint of the state is within 0.01 rad (metres for a prismatic joint) of it. Joints compare modulo a full turn, so a joint exactly one turn away from the SRDF value also counts as at the pose.
  • HOLD stops a pose move. Pressing HOLD cancels the move ("Stopping the move to stand…"), and the press does not engage, even if you keep your finger down. Once the move has ended and Servo is resumed, usually well under a second later, the status line reads "Pose move stopped. Press HOLD again.": press HOLD again to move the arm. The arm stops where it is, so the button reads "Poses" until the arm reaches a pose.
  • The background, opening the diagnostics, closing the arm view and the free-time stop cancel the move too, and resume Servo.
  • 30 s after the pick a move that has not ended is cancelled. When move_group does not end a cancel within 5 s, the arm view stops waiting for it.

Cancels need the link

Conduit cancels a move by sending the cancel to move_group, which only works while the link is up. A move running when Wi-Fi drops completes on the host. After the reconnect, the status line reads "Waiting for the move to stand to end…": HOLD stays off and Servo stays paused until the joint states show the arm still for a second (counted from 6 s after the pick, while move_group may still be planning), or 30 s after the pick. Then Conduit resumes Servo.

If the app is killed and opened again while its move still runs, the new arm view knows nothing about that move: it resumes Servo when it connects and allows HOLD while the arm may still be moving. Keep the arm's own emergency stop within reach.

docs.title: Host side
docs.text:
1. Make move_group publish the SRDF. The move_group.launch.py and demo.launch.py that the MoveIt Setup Assistant generates do. A launch file that builds move_group from MoveItConfigsBuilder needs .planning_scene_monitor(publish_robot_description_semantic=True), or the parameter publish_robot_description_semantic: True on the move_group node; it is off by default in Jazzy. Check it with:

    ros2 param get /move_group publish_robot_description_semantic   # Boolean value is: True

  2. Check that move_group serves the MoveGroup action and that Servo has its pause service:

    ros2 action list | grep move_action           # /move_action
ros2 service type /servo_node/pause_servo     # std_srvs/srv/SetBool

docs.title: When a pose move fails
docs.text:
The status line says what happened, until the next pick or HOLD press:

Message What to check "move_group not found on /move_action" move_group is not running, or runs in a namespace. "move_group refused the move to stand" move_group rejected the goal; check the move_group log on the host. "move_group did not answer the move to stand" move_group did not accept the goal, or end a cancel, within 5 s: it hangs or restarted. "The move to stand failed: …" Planning or execution failed; the rest is MoveIt's error code (see below) and, when move_group sends one, its own message after "MoveIt:". Without either, the line reads "The move to stand failed": check the move_group log on the host. "move_group stopped the move to stand" move_group cancelled the goal itself, for example because another client sent it a goal ("…: preempted (-7)"). "The move to stand took over 30 s and was stopped" The 30 s limit. A slow arm needs states closer together. "stand is no longer in the SRDF" A pick waited for a cancel while a new SRDF dropped that state. "stand has no joint values in the SRDF" The state names no joint with one number as its value. "The move to stand was not sent: …" Conduit could not send the goal, for example "Not connected to the robot". "Waiting for the move to stand to end…" The link dropped during the move (see above).

The most useful MoveIt error codes, as the status line shows them after "The move to stand failed:":

Text Code What to do "planning failed (-1)" PLANNING_FAILED No path to the state within 5 s. Move the arm closer with HOLD, or check obstacles in the planning scene. "the pose is in collision or outside the joint limits (-27)" GOAL_STATE_INVALID The group state itself is invalid. Fix it in the SRDF. "the arm starts in collision (-10)" START_STATE_IN_COLLISION The arm is in collision where it is. Jog it clear with HOLD, then pick again. "the controller failed (-4)" CONTROL_FAILED The trajectory controllers on the host refused or aborted the trajectory. Check that they are active (ros2 control list_controllers). "timed out (-6)" TIMED_OUT Execution took longer than the controllers allow. Check the host's controllers. "unknown planning group (-15)" INVALID_GROUP_NAME move_group has no group of the name the SRDF's arm group has: its MoveIt configuration is not the SRDF it publishes.

Other codes read as their short text with the number, or "MoveIt error ".

If the checkmark does not appear after a move, the arm stopped further than 0.01 rad from the state, or the Joint states topic does not carry every joint of the state (ros2 topic echo --once /joint_states --field name).

docs.title: Example: poses that Servo can move from
docs.text:
Servo stops at a singularity ("Halted: singularity" on the Servo chip) and near the joint limits ("Halted: joint bound"). An arm's ready or home state can be singular, and then HOLD does not move the arm after a pick of it. On the six-joint desk arm below (the Maker Arm), both are: the Jacobian condition number at the gripper is 35.2 at ready and 42.2 at home, above Servo's hard_stop_singularity_threshold of 30. Give the arm group states away from singularities and joint limits, and list them first, so they are the first entries of the menu. On that arm, two such states, work and stand, sit before ready and home:

<group_state name="work" group="arm">
    <joint name="link_002_joint" value="0"/>
    <joint name="link_003_joint" value="-0.95"/>
    <joint name="link_004_joint" value="1.2"/>
    <joint name="link_005_joint" value="-0.7"/>
    <joint name="link_006_joint" value="-0.1"/>
    <joint name="link_007_joint" value="0"/>
</group_state>
<group_state name="stand" group="arm">
    <joint name="link_002_joint" value="0"/>
    <joint name="link_003_joint" value="-1.6"/>
    <joint name="link_004_joint" value="1.6"/>
    <joint name="link_005_joint" value="-1.25"/>
    <joint name="link_006_joint" value="0"/>
    <joint name="link_007_joint" value="0"/>
</group_state>

That arm's menu lists work, stand, ready and home, in that order. The condition number is 25.4 at work and 21.7 at stand: between Servo's lower_singularity_threshold (17) and the hard stop, so Servo moves along every axis and slows down near them. To check a state, pick it, wait for the checkmark, hold HOLD and move the device along each axis: the Servo chip should say TWIST or "Slowing: …", not "Halted: …". The values are the desk arm's, measured in simulation; find your arm's with the arm in place, its joints well inside their limits plus Servo's joint_limit_margins.

docs.title: iPad and Mac
docs.text:
An iPad drives the arm like an iPhone, always in the two-handed layout. iPadOS pauses ARKit while Conduit shares the screen with other apps (Split View or a window); the tracking chip then reads "Camera paused: use Conduit full screen", and HOLD stops working until Conduit is full screen again. The diagnostics open in a sheet.

A Mac has no ARKit world tracking, so its arm view is view-only: the wrist camera (pinch and drag work, and it opens on the whole image), the Servo status from the profile's Servo status topic, and the diagnostics, with "Arm control needs an iPhone or iPad. This view shows the wrist camera, Servo and diagnostics." There is no HOLD, gripper, Align or pose menu, and the view pauses no sensors and does not start Device Pose.

docs.title: Servo overlay
docs.text:
conduit_teleop installs a MoveIt Servo parameter overlay at share/conduit_teleop/config/servo_overlay.yaml (source: ros/conduit_teleop/config/servo_overlay.yaml). Build conduit_teleop as described in Teleoperation to get it.

/**:
  ros__parameters:
    moveit_servo:
      incoming_command_timeout: 0.5
      command_in_type: "speed_units"
parameter value what it does moveit_servo.command_in_type speed_units Servo reads the twist as m/s and rad/s, which is what Conduit sends (not unitless −1 … 1 commands). moveit_servo.incoming_command_timeout 0.5 Servo drops a twist whose header.stamp is older than this on the host clock (default 0.1 s). Conduit stamps its twists on the robot's clock and they cross Wi-Fi, so 0.1 s drops many of them; 0.5 s keeps them, and a lost link stops the arm within about half a second (see Time sync above). Releasing the clutch stops the arm at once with explicit zero twists.

The /** key applies the file to any node, so it works whatever your launch file names the Servo node.

Load it after your robot's own Servo parameters. A node applies its parameter sources in order, so the last one wins:

from launch.substitutions import PathJoinSubstitution
from launch_ros.actions import Node
from launch_ros.substitutions import FindPackageShare

servo_node = Node(
    package="moveit_servo", executable="servo_node", name="servo_node",
    parameters=[servo_params, robot_description, robot_description_semantic,
                robot_description_kinematics,
                PathJoinSubstitution([FindPackageShare("conduit_teleop"), "config", "servo_overlay.yaml"])],
)

Check that it took effect (with your Servo node's name):

ros2 param get /servo_node moveit_servo.incoming_command_timeout   # Double value is: 0.5
ros2 param get /servo_node moveit_servo.command_in_type            # String value is: speed_units

docs.title: Drive a mobile robot
docs.text:
Coming in Conduit 3

Robots is part of Conduit 3, which is not on the App Store yet. The Conduit on the App Store today (2.x) publishes sensors but has no robot button. This page describes Robots as it will ship in Conduit 3.

Conduit sends sensor_msgs/Joy at 50 Hz while the drive view is open and the robot link is up, reliable with KEEP_LAST 1, on the profile's Joy output topic (default /joy). The layout is that of the ROS 2 joy package's game_controller_node, so teleop_twist_joy reads it as it reads a gamepad.

docs.title: iPhone
docs.text:
The drive view follows how you hold the phone: landscape for two hands, upright for one. Turn the phone to switch; with the system's rotation lock on, it stays upright. A turn lets go of every input, so press again to drive.

  • Landscape: status chips at the top left, the gear and close at the top right. At the bottom, the joystick is under one thumb (the left one unless you change it in the gear panel), the mini map is in the other corner, and the status banner is between them.
  • Upright: the same top row, the status banner above the bottom row, the joystick in the bottom corner of the hand that holds the phone (the right hand unless you change it), and the mini map in the other corner.

The chips show the battery, the speed from the odometry, the camera's latency and frame rate (the frame rate only when the robot's and the phone's clocks disagree; "No video" before the first frame; red while the camera is STALE) and the diagnostics (tap it for the full list). The battery, speed and diagnostics chips appear once they have a value. Pinch the camera to scale it between the whole image and filling the screen, and drag to pan it; Conduit keeps the zoom for each orientation. The mini map shows when the profile has a Map or LaserScan topic; tap it for the full-screen map.

docs.title: iPad and Mac
docs.text: The camera fills two thirds of the width, next to a column of Map, Status and Diagnostics tiles. Drag the divider between them to resize (the camera keeps at least 40 % of the width); double-tap it to restore the default. Tap a tile to open it in a sheet. Pinch and drag the camera to zoom it within its tile. With a hardware keyboard connected, the hint "Space + arrows or WASD to drive" shows above the banner. In a narrow iPad window the drive view uses the iPhone's landscape layout.

docs.title: Gear panel
docs.text:
• Max speed: 25%, 50%, 75% or 100% of the stick's full travel, for the forward speed and the turn rate alike. It applies to the on-screen joystick, the keyboard and a game controller's left stick. Every drive view opens at 50%. Changing it while you drive releases every input until you press again, so the robot never jumps to the new speed.
  • Stick (iPhone, landscape): Left thumb or Right thumb for the joystick.
  • Hand (iPhone, upright): Left hand or Right hand, the hand that holds the phone.

Conduit keeps the Stick and Hand choices per robot on this device. The robot keeps driving while the gear panel is open.

docs.title: Map and navigation goals
docs.text:
The full-screen map (a sheet on iPad and Mac) pinch-zooms between 0.5× and 20×, pans with a drag, and resets with a double tap. Nothing drives while the map, Status or Diagnostics is open; the banner says "Paused while a panel is open", and after you close it every input needs a fresh press.

To send a navigation goal, set the profile's Goal pose topic (/goal_pose for Nav2). The profile also needs a Map topic. Then, on the full-screen map:

  1. Tap Set goal.
  2. Touch the goal and drag toward the heading the robot should face. A tap without a drag points the goal away from the robot.

Conduit sends one geometry_msgs/PoseStamped in the profile's Map frame, with a zero stamp (the latest transform), like RViz's 2D Goal Pose tool, and then returns to panning. It waits up to 2 s for a subscriber and then sends anyway. The map says "Goal sent on <topic>", or "Goal sent, but nothing subscribes to <topic>" when no subscriber matched. The goal stays on the map until you close the drive view.

Conduit cannot cancel a goal. Releasing the joystick, closing the map or closing the drive view does not stop the robot driving to it.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
input Joy field role stick up / down axes[1] (up +) linear.x stick left / right axes[0] (left +) angular.z touching the stick, Space, or the left shoulder buttons[9] deadman (enable_button) right shoulder buttons[10] not used: turbo is off, and Conduit masks it unless the deadman is held

See Joy layout for every axis and button.

  • On-screen joystick: the touch input in every case, also with VoiceOver and with a game controller connected. Touch it to drive and lift your finger to stop.
  • Game controllers (MFi and other GameController devices): hold LB / L1 and use the left stick. The "Game controller" chip next to the joystick shows that one is connected; you can use either.
