  • Hardware keyboard (Mac, or an iPad with a keyboard): hold Space and use the arrows or WASD. The keys drive at the max speed.
  • VoiceOver: the joystick takes direct touch. It is labelled "Drive joystick" with the hint "Drag to drive; lift your finger to stop", and VoiceOver announces "Driving" and "Stopped".
  • After a lost link, the app going to the background, a closed panel, a turn of the phone or a max speed change, nothing drives until you let go of every input and press again; while you still hold one, the banner says "Release and touch again to drive". While the link is down it says "Disconnected", and while Conduit is inactive "Paused while Conduit is inactive".
  • Without Conduit Plus, a chip over the camera shows the week's free-time notices; tap it to dismiss it. When the free time runs out, the robot stops and the drive view stays behind the Conduit Plus paywall until you close it.
  • The Game Controller sensor publishes <namespace>/joy (/conduit/joy by default); the drive view publishes the profile's Joy output topic (/joy by default). Run conduit_teleop on one of them, not both. If the profile's Joy output is the sensor's topic and the sensor is enabled, Conduit asks before it opens the drive view and pauses the sensor while the drive view is open.

docs.title: Host setup
docs.text:
Install conduit_teleop as described in Teleoperation → Host setup and run it with its default joy_topic (/joy) as described in Teleoperation → Drive view.

conduit_teleop runs teleop_twist_joy with Conduit's parameter file and a watchdog. With the shipped file, full stick is 0.5 m/s and 1.0 rad/s, so the default max speed of 50% tops out at 0.25 m/s and 0.5 rad/s. The watchdog forwards teleop_twist_joy's Twist to cmd_vel while the newest Joy is younger than 0.5 s. When the Joy goes stale it publishes zero twists at 10 Hz for 1 s and then stays silent until Joy resumes (it is also silent before the first Joy), so it does not fight Nav2 or another cmd_vel publisher.

docs.title: Kachaka
docs.text:
The kachaka-api ROS 2 bridge takes velocity on /kachaka/manual_control/cmd_vel once manual control is enabled. On the host, run conduit_teleop's Kachaka launch file, which sets both up and drives at Kachaka's own speeds (Teleoperation → Kachaka). It starts conduit_teleop itself, so use it instead of conduit_teleop.launch.py, not together with it:

ros2 launch conduit_teleop kachaka.launch.py

Profile: Camera /kachaka/front_camera/image_raw/compressed, Map /kachaka/mapping/map, Map frame map, Base frame base_footprint, Goal pose /kachaka/goal_pose, the LaserScan, Odometry and Battery topics the bridge lists, Joy output /joy.

docs.title: Robots
docs.text:
Coming in Conduit 3

Robots is part of Conduit 3, which is not on the App Store yet. The Conduit on the App Store today (2.x) publishes sensors but has no robot button. This page describes Robots as it will ship in Conduit 3.

Conduit 3.0 subscribes as well as publishes. A robot profile says which topics hold the robot's camera, map, odometry, battery and diagnostics, and where Conduit sends its commands. Open shows the drive view:

  • Mobile robots — camera, map with the robot's pose and LaserScan, status and diagnostics; drive with the on-screen joystick, a game controller or a hardware keyboard, and set a navigation goal on the map. Conduit sends sensor_msgs/Joy; conduit_teleop turns it into cmd_vel.
  • Robot arms — hold HOLD and move your iPhone or iPad: a MoveIt Servo arm follows, while the screen shows the wrist camera, the gripper, diagnostics and a menu that moves the arm to the poses of its SRDF. On a Mac the arm view only watches.

docs.title: Demo videos
docs.text:
Sneak peeks of Conduit 3: a robot driven from the iPhone through its own camera, and a MoveIt Servo arm that follows the iPhone.

Drive a mobile robotCamera, map and joystick in the drive view. See Mobile robots. Move a robot armHold HOLD and move the iPhone; MoveIt Servo follows. See Robot arms.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A ROS 2 host (Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical or Rolling) reachable over Zenoh or DDS with the same settings Conduit already uses for publishing: Transport, Domain ID and Distribution in Settings. One connection serves the whole app.
  • On the host: conduit_teleop for mobile robots, and Nav2 (or another node that takes a geometry_msgs/PoseStamped goal) for map goals. For arms, MoveIt Servo from Jazzy or later and the Servo overlay, plus a move_group that publishes the SRDF if you want the pose menu.

docs.title: Where to find it
docs.text:
Tap the robot button in the toolbar, before Recordings and Settings. It is in the same place on iPhone, iPad and Mac. The Robots list opens as a sheet, with the Start button in its bottom corner as on the main screen.

Each robot in the list shows a glyph for its kind, its name, its kind (Mobile robot or Arm), a status line and Open. Tap a robot to edit it; swipe it to delete it.

docs.title: Create a profile
docs.text:
1. Tap +. The editor opens with Kind set to Mobile robot; switch it to Arm for a robot arm. Give the robot a name.

  2. Tap Start in the bottom corner (while Conduit is offline, a "Discover your robot" tip points at it). Conduit goes online and fills in the new profile from the robot:

    • each empty topic field that has exactly one discovered topic of the right type, including Servo's twist topic, command type service and status topic, and the gripper action;
    • the frames: for a mobile robot the Map frame from the map and the Base frame from the odometry; for an arm the Base frame, the Gripper joint and the gripper's Open and Closed positions from the robot's SRDF and URDF.

    Each field is filled once. A field you type in or clear stays as you left it, and a saved profile is never filled again. The list button next to a field shows every discovered topic that fits it.

  3. Check the fields. An empty field shows a usual name in grey. Joy output and Goal pose are never discovered, because only the robot subscribes to them: type them if the grey name is wrong. Under Required topics, an empty field is saved as the grey default. Under Optional topics, an empty field turns off what it feeds.

  4. Tap Save. An arm's named poses are not part of the profile: the arm view's pose menu lists the group states of the robot's SRDF; see Named poses.

If Conduit finds no topics, the editor shows "No topics found" with the likely causes: the Distribution (Humble vs Jazzy and later), the domain ID, the Zenoh router or the DDS peers, and the profile's connection. You can still type the topic names.

A profile remembers the connection it was made with. If the app uses a different transport or domain, or Humble where the profile was made for a later distribution (or the reverse), the Robots list and the drive view say so ("Profile expects DDS · domain 123 · Jazzy"). The list offers Stop & edit settings, and the editor offers Use the app settings for this profile. Jazzy and the later distributions share one wire format, so switching between them raises no warning. Under each robot the list also shows Offline, how many of the profile's topics are live ("3 of 5 topics live"), or, for an arm, "Servo not found".

docs.title: Open
docs.text:
The Start button is the app's one online switch. Open on an offline app starts it in Publish mode with the sensors you have enabled (none is fine), and so does Start in the Robots list and the editor. If a recording is running offline, Conduit asks "Publish & Record?" first. If the week's free time is used up, the Conduit Plus paywall opens instead of the drive view.

The drive view comes up the way you hold the device and turns with it; the system's rotation lock keeps it as it is. On iPhone, landscape is the two-handed layout and upright the one-handed one, and closing the drive view turns the screen back to portrait. On iPad the arm view always uses the two-handed layout. On iPad and Mac the mobile drive view shows the camera next to Map, Status and Diagnostics tiles (in a narrow window, the iPhone's landscape layout).

Close (×) ends what the drive view started. The app stays online until you tap Stop on the Start button. The drive view also closes when the app goes offline: when the first connection fails, or when the app goes to the background with Background Publishing off.

docs.title: Free time and Conduit Plus
docs.text:
Robots is part of the free plan's 5 hours of use a week. A drive view counts while its robot link is connected; a ROS 2 subscriber to Conduit's topics and a running recording count too. On iPhone and iPad, time counts only while Conduit is in the foreground; a Mac counts in the background too. Each device has its own time, and it refills on Monday at 00:00 local time. The dial around the Start button shows what is left: orange at 30 minutes, red at 5 minutes. Conduit Plus removes the limit.

When the time runs out in a drive view, a held stick, a held HOLD or a running pose move gets up to 5 more minutes to end. Conduit then sends its stop commands, closes a running recording, stops, and shows the paywall over the stopped drive view. Closing the paywall returns you to the Robots list.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Conduit is not an emergency stop

Releasing the drive controls stops Conduit's commands. That cannot stop a robot whose controller keeps the last command, and it does nothing when the network is gone. Keep the robot's own emergency stop within reach.

  • Mobile robots: letting go of the stick, the game controller or the keys sends Joy with the enable button released. Opening the map, status or diagnostics panel and the app going to the background do the same; after them, and after a lost link, driving needs a fresh press. Run conduit_teleop: its watchdog forwards velocity commands while the newest /joy is younger than 0.5 s. When Joy goes stale, for example because the phone dropped off Wi-Fi, it publishes zero velocity at 10 Hz for 1 s and then stays silent until Joy resumes (it is also silent before the first Joy), so the robot stops without the watchdog fighting Nav2. A map goal is a plain topic message: Conduit cannot cancel it.
  • Arms: releasing HOLD sends zero twists at once. If the link is lost, Servo stops on its command timeout (0.5 s with the overlay). Conduit stamps every twist, the zero ones included, on the robot's clock, which it reads from the profile's Joint states topic, so the stop does not depend on the device's clock being right. HOLD stays off until that clock is known (time sync). A named-pose move is planned and run by move_group on the host. Pressing HOLD, opening the diagnostics, closing the arm view and the app going to the background cancel it, and so does a move that has not ended after 30 s. A cancel needs the link: a move running when Wi-Fi drops completes on the host, and after the reconnect Conduit keeps HOLD off until the arm has stopped, or for at most 30 s from the pick.

docs.title: When something is wrong
docs.text: What you see What to check "No topics found" in the profile editor Distribution (Humble vs Jazzy and later), domain ID, the Zenoh router or DDS peers, the profile's connection "Robot link lost" in the profile editor The link is down ("Router connection lost", "No data from the robot" or "Robot publishers left the graph"); Conduit keeps retrying "Servo not found" in the Robots list Nothing publishes the arm profile's Servo status topic: Servo is not running, or the profile names another node "No data — check Distribution / QoS" The topic exists but nothing arrives: a type mismatch from the wrong Distribution, or QoS "No TF <map frame> → <base frame>" (for example "No TF map → base_footprint") The map → base transform is not published; the map and scan still show. It appears once the map has arrived "Unsupported encoding: X" The camera publishes an encoding Conduit does not draw. It draws JPEG and PNG CompressedImage, and Image in rgb8, bgr8, rgba8, bgra8 and mono8 "Disconnected" in the mobile drive view, "Connecting…" in the arm view's status line The link is down; Conduit reconnects with backoff. Driving needs a fresh touch afterwards, and HOLD a fresh press Red STALE over the camera No camera frame for 0.5 s. The last image stays, dimmed, until frames come back, and the camera chip turns red Camera at 15 fps, or "Paused — device is hot" / "Camera paused: the device is too hot" The device is hot: the camera is drawn at 15 fps when it is seriously hot and stops drawing when it is critically hot. Control is never slowed down "Camera paused: use Conduit full screen" in the iPad arm view iPadOS pauses motion tracking while Conduit shares the screen with other apps. Use Conduit full screen

docs.title: Sensors and topics
docs.text: This page lists what Conduit publishes. Topic names use the default namespace conduit; if you change Namespace in Settings, replace /conduit with yours.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text:
Sensor Topic Message type Default rate Max rate Platforms IMU /conduit/imu sensor_msgs/msg/Imu 100 Hz 100 Hz iPhone, iPad Magnetic Field /conduit/magnetic_field sensor_msgs/msg/MagneticField 100 Hz 100 Hz iPhone, iPad Barometer /conduit/barometer sensor_msgs/msg/FluidPressure 10 Hz 10 Hz iPhone, iPad Illuminance /conduit/illuminance sensor_msgs/msg/Illuminance 10 Hz 10 Hz iPhone, iPad GPS /conduit/fix sensor_msgs/msg/NavSatFix 1 Hz 10 Hz iPhone, iPad Proximity /conduit/range sensor_msgs/msg/Range 10 Hz 10 Hz iPhone Device Pose (Conduit 3) /conduit/pose and /tf geometry_msgs/msg/PoseStamped 60 Hz 60 Hz iPhone, iPad Camera /conduit/camera/<camera>/image_raw/compressed sensor_msgs/msg/CompressedImage 30 Hz 60 Hz iPhone, iPad, Mac LiDAR /conduit/points sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 30 Hz 60 Hz iPhone Pro, iPad Pro Microphone /conduit/audio audio_common_msgs/msg/AudioData 16 Hz 16 Hz iPhone, iPad, Mac Battery /conduit/battery_state sensor_msgs/msg/BatteryState 1 Hz 10 Hz iPhone, iPad, Mac Thermal /conduit/temperature sensor_msgs/msg/Temperature 1 Hz 10 Hz iPhone, iPad, Mac Game Controller /conduit/joy sensor_msgs/msg/Joy 50 Hz 60 Hz iPhone, iPad, Mac

Every sensor is off until you turn it on. To change a sensor's rate or QoS, stop publishing and tap the settings button under its toggle. See Platform notes for which devices have which sensors.

Notes on some sensors:

  • IMU follows REP-145: linear_acceleration includes gravity (+9.81 m/s² on the up axis at rest), and orientation is relative to ENU with magnetic east. Conduit does not correct for magnetic declination; correct it on the host if you need true north (for example with magnetic_declination_radians in navsat_transform_node).
  • Illuminance is estimated from the camera's exposure. It uses the camera, so it cannot run together with a camera stream, LiDAR or Device Pose; Conduit asks before it turns the other one off.
  • Thermal is an estimate from the system thermal state (nominal, fair, serious, critical), not a temperature sensor reading.
  • Proximity is a near/far reading from the sensor at the top of the iPhone's screen.
  • Microphone sends 16 kHz, mono, 16-bit signed little-endian samples, 1024 samples per message. AudioData has no header. See the FAQ for how to receive it.
  • Game Controller uses the layout of the ROS 2 joy package's game_controller_node. See Teleoperation.
  • Device Pose (Conduit 3) uses ARKit world tracking. It publishes only while tracking is normal. It cannot run together with Illuminance or with a camera stream, except the wide camera while LiDAR is on.

docs.title: Camera topics
docs.text:
Each camera publishes on its own topics under /conduit/camera/<camera>/:

Camera <camera> Optical frame Front front camera_front_optical_frame Wide (back) wide camera_back_optical_frame Ultra Wide (back) ultrawide camera_ultrawide_optical_frame Telephoto (back) telephoto camera_telephoto_optical_frame

You see only the cameras your device has. You can turn on several at once. The front camera is free; the back cameras need the Back Cameras In-App Purchase. On a Mac, Conduit uses the built-in FaceTime HD camera only.

Each camera's settings sheet has:

  • Output: Compressed publishes JPEG images on image_raw/compressed (sensor_msgs/msg/CompressedImage). Raw publishes uncompressed bgra8 images on image_raw (sensor_msgs/msg/Image). Raw images are much larger, so use them on a fast network.
  • Resolution: QVGA (320 × 240), VGA (640 × 480, the default), 720p (1280 × 720) or 1080p (1920 × 1080). The image is rotated to match the Mounting setting.
  • JPEG Quality: 10 to 100 %, 80 % by default (Compressed only).
  • Rate and QoS.

Each camera also publishes camera_info (sensor_msgs/msg/CameraInfo) for the published image size. Conduit uses the camera's calibration when iOS provides it, and otherwise estimates the intrinsics from the field of view. camera_info is latched, so a subscriber that joins late still receives it.

Higher resolutions and quality settings can lower the achieved frame rate.

docs.title: LiDAR
docs.text:
LiDAR needs an iPhone 12 Pro or later Pro model, or an iPad Pro (2020 or later), and the LiDAR In-App Purchase. It uses ARKit, which provides only the wide back camera: while LiDAR is on, only the wide camera streams, and turning on another camera turns LiDAR off (Conduit asks first).

The LiDAR settings sheet has an Output setting:

Output Publishes Point Cloud (default) /conduit/points (sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2, fields x, y, z, in lidar_link) Depth /conduit/camera/wide/depth/image_raw (sensor_msgs/msg/Image, 16UC1, millimeters, 0 = no depth) and /conduit/camera/wide/depth/camera_info Both All of the above

The depth image is aligned with the wide camera and uses camera_back_optical_frame. With the wide camera also on, LiDAR mode takes the color image from ARKit and publishes it on /conduit/camera/wide/image_raw/compressed with /conduit/camera/wide/camera_info. In LiDAR mode the color image is always compressed; the camera's resolution, JPEG quality and rate settings still apply.

Messages from the same ARKit frame carry the same header.stamp, the time ARKit captured the frame. Match a color image with its depth image by equal stamps. See Capture an RGB and depth pair.

The depth topics use the LiDAR sensor's QoS, which is best effort by default. Nodes that subscribe reliably, such as depth_image_proc, need the LiDAR QoS set to Reliable, or a best-effort QoS override on the subscriber.

docs.title: Point cloud compression
docs.text:
With Enable Compression on, Conduit publishes /conduit/points/compressed (point_cloud_interfaces/msg/CompressedPointCloud2) instead of /conduit/points. Formats:

  • Draco: lossy, best compression ratio.
  • Zstd (default): lossless, good balance of speed and ratio.
  • Zlib: lossless.

Level goes from 1 to 9 (default 5). Higher levels compress more and take longer.

docs.title: Frames and TF
docs.text:
Conduit publishes the transforms between its frames on /tf_static (tf2_msgs/msg/TFMessage). It is a global topic, not under the namespace. It is latched (reliable, transient local), so tools that start later, such as RViz, still receive it.

All frames are children of conduit_base_link:

  • conduit_base_link: x forward (where the back camera looks), y left, z up (REP-103). The origin is at the IMU.
  • imu_link, magnetometer_link, barometer_link, thermal_link, battery_link: at the origin, same axes.
  • gps_link, microphone_link, illuminance_link: same axes as conduit_base_link.
  • lidar_link: same axes as conduit_base_link, at the wide camera. /conduit/points is in this frame.
  • proximity_link: x points out of the screen, because sensor_msgs/Range measures along x.
  • camera_back_optical_frame, camera_ultrawide_optical_frame, camera_telephoto_optical_frame, camera_front_optical_frame: optical frames (x right, y down, z forward) in the published image.

Sensor offsets are approximate, based on an iPhone 14 Pro.

The Mounting setting (Settings → ROS 2 Node) says how the device is held. In both options the back camera faces forward (+x):

  • Portrait: top of the phone up.
  • Landscape: top of the phone to the left.

Pick the one that matches how the device is mounted on your robot. Mounting changes the frames, the IMU axes and the image rotation together. You cannot change it while publishing or recording.

docs.title: Device Pose frames (Conduit 3)
docs.text: Device Pose publishes conduit_base_link in conduit_odom on /conduit/pose and on /tf (a global topic). conduit_odom is gravity aligned with z up; its origin and yaw are the device pose when the ARKit session started. A pose carries the stamp of the ARKit frame it came from, so it shares the stamp with color and depth images from the same frame. Not every image has a pose: poses pause while tracking is not normal.

docs.title: QoS defaults
docs.text:
Topics Reliability Durability History Sensor topics Best effort Volatile Keep last 10 /conduit/joy Reliable Volatile Keep last 10 camera_info (camera without LiDAR) Best effort Transient local Keep last 1 /tf_static Reliable Transient local Keep last 1

You can change Reliability (Best Effort / Reliable) and History Depth (1 to 100) per sensor. A subscriber that asks for reliable delivery does not receive a best-effort topic; subscribe with best effort (qos_profile_sensor_data in rclpy, --qos-reliability best_effort with ros2 topic), or set the sensor to Reliable.

The Game Controller is reliable by default because joy consumers such as teleop_twist_joy subscribe reliably.

To send data only while a subscriber is connected, turn on Publish only when subscribed. See On-demand capture.

docs.title: Namespace and node name
docs.text:
Settings → ROS 2 Node:

  • Node Name: conduit_node by default.
  • Namespace: conduit by default. Every sensor topic is under it, for example /conduit/imu. /tf_static and /tf are always global.

docs.title: Teleoperation with a game controller
docs.text:
Requires Conduit 2.5 or later

The Joy layout and the setup on this page need Conduit 2.5 or later. Settings → About & Help shows your version. Conduit 2.4 and earlier publish an older Joy layout with Best Effort QoS (see the next box).

Conduit's Game Controller sensor publishes sensor_msgs/msg/Joy from any controller paired with your iPhone, iPad or Mac (Xbox, PlayStation, MFi). It publishes on /conduit/joy: the sensor's topic is joy, under Conduit's namespace, which is conduit unless you changed Settings → Namespace (then it is /<namespace>/joy). That is why the commands below pass joy_topic:=/conduit/joy. (Conduit 3.0's drive view uses /joy instead.) On the robot, teleop_twist_joy turns the Joy messages into velocity commands. This page sets that up with conduit_teleop, a ROS 2 package in this repository.

Conduit 2.5 changes the Joy message to the ROS 2 joy layout

From Conduit 2.5, Game Controller publishes Joy exactly like the ROS 2 joy package's game_controller_node. Compared with Conduit 2.4 and earlier:

  • Stick X axes: left is now +1 (it was −1). The Y axes are unchanged (up = +1).
  • Triggers: 0 when released and −1 when fully pressed. They were 0 … +1.
  • D-pad: moved from axes[6] / axes[7] to buttons[11]–buttons[14]. axes now has 6 entries.
  • Buttons: follow the SDL order in the table below. buttons has 21 entries.
  • QoS: Reliable by default, which teleop_twist_joy needs. If you saved Best Effort for the Game Controller in an earlier version, Conduit switches it to Reliable once. You can set it back in the sensor's settings.

If your robot remaps axes or inverts signs to make an earlier Conduit drive correctly, remove that remapping. Otherwise the robot turns the wrong way.

docs.title: Joy layout
docs.text:
The layout is the one that game_controller_node publishes in ROS 2 Jazzy (joy 3.3.0).

index axes[i] value 0 left stick, left / right left = +1, right = −1 1 left stick, up / down up = +1, down = −1 2 right stick, left / right left = +1, right = −1 3 right stick, up / down up = +1, down = −1 4 left trigger released 0, fully pressed −1 5 right trigger released 0, fully pressed −1 index buttons[i] Xbox PlayStation 0 A A Cross 1 B B Circle 2 X X Square 3 Y Y Triangle 4 Back View Share / Create 5 Guide Xbox button PS button 6 Start Menu Options 7 Left stick press LS L3 8 Right stick press RS R3 9 Left shoulder LB L1 10 Right shoulder RB R1 11–14 D-pad up, down, left, right 15–20 always 0

A Siri Remote (Apple TV remote) sends its touch surface as the left stick (axes[0], axes[1]), and its A, X and Menu buttons as buttons[0], buttons[2] and buttons[6].

Conduit publishes Joy at 50 Hz while a controller is connected, and stops when the controller disconnects.

docs.title: Host setup with conduit_teleop
docs.text:
/conduit/joy ──► teleop_twist_joy ──► cmd_vel_in ──► joy_watchdog ──► /cmd_vel
      │                                                   ▲
      └──────────────── Joy freshness ────────────────────┘
  • teleop_twist_joy uses config/teleop_twist_joy.yaml, or the file you pass as params_file. Hold LB / L1 (buttons[9]) to drive. The left stick's up / down sets linear.x and its left / right sets angular.z. Releasing LB sends one zero twist. Turbo is off, because teleop_twist_joy checks the turbo button before the deadman, so a turbo button would drive the robot without LB held.
  • joy_watchdog forwards the twist while the newest Joy is younger than 0.5 s. When Joy stops arriving, it publishes a zero twist at 10 Hz for 1 s and then goes quiet until Joy comes back. That happens when Wi-Fi drops, the controller disconnects, or Conduit goes to the background. teleop_twist_joy alone would leave a robot that keeps its last command moving.

docs.title: Install (ROS 2 Jazzy)
docs.text:
sudo apt install ros-jazzy-teleop-twist-joy
mkdir -p ~/conduit_ws/src
git clone https://github.com/youtalk/conduit-support.git ~/conduit_ws/src/conduit-support
cd ~/conduit_ws
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
colcon build --packages-select conduit_teleop
source install/setup.bash

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
ros2 launch conduit_teleop conduit_teleop.launch.py joy_topic:=/conduit/joy
argument default meaning joy_topic /joy Joy input. The Game Controller sensor publishes /conduit/joy (namespace conduit), so pass joy_topic:=/conduit/joy, or /<namespace>/joy if you changed the namespace. cmd_vel_topic /cmd_vel Where the robot listens for geometry_msgs/Twist. params_file the package's config/teleop_twist_joy.yaml The teleop_twist_joy parameter file. It replaces the shipped file, so start from a copy of it.

At full stick the robot drives at 0.5 m/s and turns at 1.0 rad/s. To change that for your robot, copy the shipped file, change scale_linear.x and scale_angular.yaw in the copy, and pass it as params_file:

cp ~/conduit_ws/src/conduit-support/ros/conduit_teleop/config/teleop_twist_joy.yaml ~/my_robot_teleop.yaml
ros2 launch conduit_teleop conduit_teleop.launch.py joy_topic:=/conduit/joy params_file:=$HOME/my_robot_teleop.yaml

Keep the rest of the copy as it is, including the teleop_twist_joy_node: key. A parameter the file leaves out falls back to teleop_twist_joy's own default, which is not this layout (its default deadman is buttons[5]). To try a speed without restarting, ros2 param set /teleop_twist_joy_node scale_linear.x 0.3 changes the running node.

joy_watchdog parameter default meaning timeout 0.5 Seconds without a Joy before the watchdog takes over. zero_rate_hz 10.0 Rate of the zero twist once Joy is stale. zero_duration 1.0 Seconds of zero twists after Joy goes stale; then the watchdog is silent until Joy comes back.

Sharing cmd_vel_topic with Nav2 or another teleop

joy_watchdog publishes only while you drive and for 1 s after Joy stops, so it does not keep overriding another node once you let go. While you drive, both would publish to the same topic, so for a robot that also runs Nav2 or a second teleop, feed both into twist_mux and use the mux input as cmd_vel_topic.

Not an emergency stop

Neither Conduit nor conduit_teleop is a safety system. Keep the robot's own emergency stop within reach.

docs.title: Drive view
docs.text:
Requires Conduit 3.0

The drive view is part of Robots, which Conduit 3.0 adds. The Game Controller sensor above works from Conduit 2.5.

Conduit 3.0's Robots drive view sends the same Joy layout at 50 Hz while it is open (reliable, KEEP_LAST 1), on the robot profile's Joy output topic, which is /joy by default. For it, launch conduit_teleop with the default joy_topic:

ros2 launch conduit_teleop conduit_teleop.launch.py

The two Joy sources use different topics: the drive view publishes /joy, the Game Controller sensor /conduit/joy. Point conduit_teleop at one of them, not both: the default joy_topic to drive from the drive view, joy_topic:=/conduit/joy to drive with the Game Controller sensor. If you set a profile's Joy output to the sensor's topic, Conduit asks before it opens the drive view and pauses the sensor while the drive view is open.

In the drive view, touching the on-screen joystick (or holding Space on a hardware keyboard, or LB / L1 on a controller) holds buttons[9]. The gear panel's Max speed (25%, 50%, 75% or 100%) scales the stick on the phone, for both the forward and the turn rate. At 100% the parameter file's scales are the top speeds; every drive view opens at 50%, half of them. The watchdog behaves the same for both sources. See Drive a mobile robot for the drive view itself.

docs.title: Kachaka
docs.text:
The kachaka-api ROS 2 bridge takes velocity on /kachaka/manual_control/cmd_vel while manual control is enabled. kachaka.launch.py starts conduit_teleop for it, so run it instead of conduit_teleop.launch.py, not together with it (both would start a teleop_twist_joy_node and a joy_watchdog with the same names):

ros2 launch conduit_teleop kachaka.launch.py
  • cmd_vel_topic is <kachaka_namespace>/manual_control/cmd_vel.
  • params_file is the package's config/kachaka_teleop_twist_joy.yaml, a full copy of teleop_twist_joy.yaml (same axes, deadman and turbo off) with full-stick speeds of 0.3 m/s and 1.57 rad/s. The bridge divides cmd_vel by exactly these maximums, so at Max speed 100% full stick is Kachaka's top speed. At the default 50% the top is 0.15 m/s and 0.79 rad/s. The default file's 0.5 m/s would ask for more than Kachaka's top speed beyond 60 % of the stick.
  • Two seconds after start it calls <kachaka_namespace>/manual_control/set_enabled with true.
argument default meaning joy_topic /joy Joy input: the drive view's Joy topic. kachaka_namespace /kachaka Namespace of the kachaka-api ROS 2 bridge.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The drive view is open but the robot does not move. Check that Joy arrives on the profile's Joy topic: ros2 topic hz /joy. Then check that conduit_teleop listens on that topic (its default joy_topic is /joy) and that you are touching the stick, which is the deadman.
  • Nothing on /cmd_vel while you hold LB, and ros2 topic hz /conduit/joy shows nothing. No Joy reaches the host. Check the topic name (ros2 topic list | grep joy), the domain ID and the transport.
  • The robot turns the wrong way. Remove any axis inversion you set up for Conduit 2.4 or earlier.
  • Nothing on /cmd_vel although Joy arrives. Hold LB (buttons[9]). Check ros2 topic echo /conduit/joy --field buttons while you press it.
  • Over DDS, nothing on /cmd_vel although ros2 topic hz /conduit/joy shows Joy. Over DDS (rmw_cyclonedds_cpp) a Best Effort Joy does not match teleop_twist_joy's Reliable subscription; keep the Game Controller sensor on Reliable. ros2 topic info -v /conduit/joy shows the publisher's reliability. Conduit 2.4 and earlier published Best Effort.

docs.title: Transports: Zenoh vs DDS
docs.text:
Conduit publishes ROS 2 messages over one of two transports. This page helps you pick one and set it up.

The easiest way to set up either one is Connect with a QR code (Conduit 2.6.0 or later): a script on your ROS 2 PC checks the setup, and scanning its QR code fills in the connection settings in Conduit.

docs.title: Quick decision
docs.text:
Your ROS 2 setup Transport Uses rmw_zenoh_cpp Zenoh Uses rmw_cyclonedds_cpp DDS Device and host on different subnets, or over the internet Zenoh (for example over Tailscale) Same LAN, and you don't want to run a router DDS Network blocks multicast or isolates Wi-Fi clients Zenoh (TCP)

The default RMW on Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical and Rolling is Fast DDS (rmw_fastrtps_cpp), so set RMW_IMPLEMENTATION on the host. A Fast DDS host can discover Conduit over DDS, but may drop or delay high-rate topics such as the camera and LiDAR.

docs.title: Side by side
docs.text:
Zenoh DDS (CycloneDDS) ROS 2 RMW rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_cyclonedds_cpp Router required Yes (rmw_zenohd) No Discovery Through the router Multicast; add peers for unicast on top (hybrid) Network traffic TCP, port 7447 by default UDP, from 7400 + 250 × domain ID Across subnets Yes No (same LAN only) Tailscale Yes No Network interface on iPhone / iPad Any that reaches the router en0 (WiFi) Domain ID 0–232 0–232 Large messages (camera, LiDAR) TCP to the router UDP fragments; busy Wi-Fi may drop them

Conduit embeds CycloneDDS 11.0.1. Use the rmw_cyclonedds_cpp that ships with your ROS 2 distribution.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Open Settings (gear icon) in Conduit. Changes are saved as you make them; tap Done to close. You cannot change the connection while publishing.

Zenoh:

  • Transport: Zenoh
  • Router Address: the IP address of the host that runs rmw_zenohd
  • Router Port: 7447
  • Domain ID: the host's ROS_DOMAIN_ID
  • Distribution: your host's ROS 2 release (Lyrical by default)

Start the router on the host:

export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd

DDS:

  • Transport: DDS

  • Discovery: opens the DDS Discovery page:

    • Peers: add the ROS 2 host's IP address. With no peers, Conduit uses multicast discovery. With peers, it also sends unicast discovery to them (hybrid).
    • Network Interface: en0 (WiFi) on iPhone and iPad.
    • This Device shows the device's IP address.

  • Domain ID: the host's ROS_DOMAIN_ID

  • Distribution: your host's ROS 2 release (Lyrical by default)

Discovery changes apply the next time you tap Start.

On the host, add the device's address (This Device) as a peer too:

export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
export CYCLONEDDS_URI='<CycloneDDS><Domain><Discovery><Peers><Peer address="DEVICE_IP"/></Peers></Discovery></Domain></CycloneDDS>'
ros2 daemon stop

Replace DEVICE_IP with the address shown under This Device. Run ros2 daemon stop after you change RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID or CYCLONEDDS_URI, so the ros2 CLI picks up the change.

docs.title: Network requirements
docs.text:
• Zenoh: the device must reach the router over TCP (port 7447 by default). Allow that port in the host's firewall.
  • DDS: the device and the host must be on the same LAN subnet, with UDP allowed on the DDS ports: 7400 + 250 × domain ID and the next 249 ports. Guest and office Wi-Fi often isolate clients from each other ("AP isolation"), which blocks DDS. Use Zenoh on such networks, or disable AP isolation.

docs.title: Tailscale
docs.text: Zenoh works over a Tailscale tailnet, so the device and the host can be on different networks. Put both on the same tailnet and use the host's Tailscale address as the Router Address. The QR code script sets this up with --tailscale; see Connect with a QR code. DDS does not work over Tailscale.

docs.title: When to switch
docs.text:
Use Zenoh if:

  • Large camera or LiDAR messages drop on DDS.
  • You need to connect from another subnet or from outside the LAN.
  • Your Wi-Fi blocks multicast or isolates clients, and you cannot change it.

Use DDS if:

  • Your ROS 2 nodes already use CycloneDDS and you don't want to run a Zenoh router.
  • You want the shortest network path, with no hop through a router.

See also:

  • FAQ: setup questions
  • Troubleshooting: problems with either transport
  • Known issues: current limitations

docs.title: Troubleshooting guide
docs.text:
Common issues and solutions for Conduit.

Connecting for the first time? Use Connect with a QR code. The script checks the ROS 2 PC (RMW, router, firewall, peers), fills in Conduit's settings, and prints what to fix when the iPhone does not check in.

Which transport are you using? Check Settings → Transport in the Conduit app. Zenoh and DDS have different failure modes. Zenoh issues are under "Connection issues" and "Topic issues" below; DDS-specific issues are in "DDS transport issues" at the bottom of this page.

docs.title: "Connection Failed: Timeout"
docs.text:
Problem: App cannot reach the Zenoh router.

Solutions:

  1. Verify router is running: 

    # On ROS 2 system
ps aux | grep rmw_zenohd

# If not running, start it
source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash   # or your distro
export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd

  2. Check IP address: 

    # Get your ROS 2 system's IP
ip addr show | grep "inet "  # Linux
ifconfig | grep "inet "      # macOS

  3. Update router address in app Settings

  4. Verify same network: iPhone and ROS 2 system must be on same WiFi/LAN

  5. Allow Local Network access: iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Local Network → Conduit must be on.

  6. Test connectivity: 

    # From iPhone, ping ROS 2 system
# Or from ROS 2 system, ping iPhone
ping <device-ip>

docs.title: "Connection Refused"
docs.text:
Problem: Router is not listening on port 7447.

Solutions:

  1. Check router is running: See "Timeout" solutions above

  2. Verify port: 

    # Check if port 7447 is listening
netstat -an | grep 7447
lsof -i :7447

  3. Check firewall: 

    # Ubuntu/Linux
sudo ufw status
sudo ufw allow 7447/tcp

# macOS
# System Settings → Network → Firewall → Allow port 7447

  4. Try different port: If 7447 is blocked, configure router with different port

docs.title: Connection drops and reconnects
docs.text:
Problem: Data stops for a while during a session, then comes back on its own.

What Conduit does: When a send fails (for example, the router restarts or Wi-Fi drops briefly), Conduit keeps running and reconnects in the background. It retries after 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds, then every 30 seconds, with no limit. Sends never block the app: while the network is stalled, Conduit drops the oldest queued messages instead of freezing. When the device loses its network entirely, Conduit stops publishing and shows Connection Lost.

Solutions:

  1. Wait: after a router restart, data usually resumes at the next retry.
  2. Check the router or host: if data does not come back, see "Connection Failed: Timeout" above.
  3. Check Wi-Fi signal: weak Wi-Fi causes repeated drops, especially with camera or LiDAR.
  4. Restart publishing: stop and start again in the app.

docs.title: "Network Unreachable"
docs.text:
Problem: No network connectivity.

Solutions:

  1. Enable WiFi on iPhone: Settings → WiFi

  2. Connect to same network as ROS 2 system

  3. Check router running: iPhone → Settings → WiFi → (i) → Router address

  4. Restart network:

  5. Toggle WiFi off/on
  6. Restart iPhone
  7. Restart router

docs.title: Topic doesn't appear in ros2 topic list
docs.text:
Problem: Conduit is publishing but topic is invisible.

Solutions:

  1. Verify domain IDs match (most common issue): 
    # Check ROS 2 system domain ID
echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID

# Check Docker container domain ID
docker exec ros_lyrical_zenoh bash -c "echo \$ROS_DOMAIN_ID"
  2. Domain ID in app Settings must match ROS_DOMAIN_ID on host
  3. Valid range: 0-232 (RTPS specification limit)

  4. Default is 0 if not set

  5. Verify RMW_IMPLEMENTATION: 

    echo $RMW_IMPLEMENTATION
# Zenoh transport: rmw_zenoh_cpp
# DDS transport:   rmw_cyclonedds_cpp (see "DDS transport issues" below)

  6. Check the Distribution setting:

  7. Set Settings → Distribution to match your host (Humble vs Jazzy and later)

  8. Restart Zenoh router: 

    # Kill existing router
pkill rmw_zenohd

# Restart with correct domain ID
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0  # Match app's domain ID
ros2 run rmw_zenoh_cpp rmw_zenohd

  9. Check app connection state: Should show "Publishing"

docs.title: Topic appears but ros2 topic echo shows no data
docs.text:
Problem: Topic exists but no messages received.

Solutions:

  1. Check for "Waiting for subscriber":
  2. If the sensor row says Waiting for subscriber, Settings → Publishing → Publish only when subscribed is on and no subscription matches the topic. The message count and rate in the next item do not apply to a waiting row.

  3. See Why does a sensor say "Waiting for subscriber"?

  4. Verify sensor is publishing:

  5. Check message count in app (should be increasing)

  6. Rate should be > 0 Hz

  7. Check QoS compatibility:

  8. App uses: Reliability=BestEffort, History=KeepLast(10) by default
  9. Game Controller (sensor_msgs/Joy) is Reliable by default

  10. Subscribe with --qos-reliability best_effort, or change the sensor's QoS in its settings

  11. Restart app: Stop and restart publishing

  12. Check the Distribution setting:

  13. Set Settings → Distribution to match your host (Humble vs Jazzy and later)

docs.title: "Camera Permission Denied"
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Grant permission:
  2. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Camera

  3. Find "Conduit" and enable

  4. Restart app after granting permission

docs.title: "LiDAR Not Available"
docs.text:
Reasons:

  1. Device doesn't have LiDAR:
  2. iPhone: iPhone 12 Pro or later Pro models
  3. iPad: iPad Pro (2020 or later)

  4. Mac: not available

  5. Camera permission required: LiDAR uses ARKit which requires camera access

  6. Purchase required: LiDAR is a one-time In-App Purchase

  7. Another camera is on: ARKit gives only the wide camera, so turning on the front, ultra-wide or telephoto camera turns LiDAR off

docs.title: "Microphone Permission Denied"
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Grant permission:
  2. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone

  3. Find "Conduit" and enable

  4. Restart app after granting permission

docs.title: "GPS Location Services Disabled"
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Enable location services:

  2. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → ON

  3. Grant app permission:

  4. iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → Conduit

  5. Select "While Using the App"

  6. Restart app

docs.title: Sensor shows 0 Hz rate
docs.text:
Problem: Sensor enabled but not publishing data.

Solutions:

  1. Check connection state: Must show "Publishing"

  2. Verify sensor permission: Check iOS Settings → Privacy

  3. Try different sensor: Test if other sensors work

  4. Restart publishing: Stop and start again

  5. Check logs: Look for error messages in app

docs.title: macOS: IMU not available
docs.text:
Expected behavior: On Mac, Conduit offers only Camera, Microphone, Battery, Thermal and Game Controller. IMU, Magnetometer, Barometer, Illuminance, GPS, Proximity, LiDAR and Device Pose are not available.

Workaround: Use an iPhone or iPad for those sensors. See Platform notes.

docs.title: ros2 topic echo /conduit/audio fails with "unknown type"
docs.text:
Problem: audio_common_msgs package is not installed on the ROS 2 system.

Solutions:

  1. Use the pre-built Docker image (includes audio_common_msgs): 

    docker run -d -p 7447:7447 --name ros_lyrical_zenoh ghcr.io/youtalk/conduit-support:lyrical
docker exec ros_lyrical_zenoh bash -c \
  "source /opt/ros/lyrical/setup.bash && \
   source /ros2_ws/install/setup.bash && \
   export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_zenoh_cpp && \
   ros2 topic echo /conduit/audio audio_common_msgs/msg/AudioData"

  2. Install on native ROS 2: 

    sudo apt install ros-lyrical-audio-common  # Lyrical
sudo apt install ros-jazzy-audio-common   # Jazzy
sudo apt install ros-humble-audio-common  # Humble

  3. Build from source if apt package is unavailable: 

    cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone --branch ros2 --depth 1 https://github.com/ros-drivers/audio_common.git
cd ~/ros2_ws && colcon build --packages-select audio_common_msgs
source install/setup.bash

docs.title: High battery drain
docs.text:
Causes:

  1. Too many sensors enabled: Disable unused sensors

  2. High publishing rates: Reduce rate for non-critical sensors

  3. Camera/LiDAR active: These consume significant power

Solutions:

  • Enable only sensors you need
  • Reduce rates (e.g., GPS 1Hz instead of 10Hz)
  • Disable camera when not needed

docs.title: App becomes unresponsive
docs.text:
Solutions:

  1. Memory warning: iOS killed background sensors
  2. Check Console logs

  3. Reduce number of active sensors

  4. Network issues: Connection lost

  5. Verify router still running
  6. Check WiFi signal strength

  7. See Connection drops and reconnects

  8. Restart app: Force quit and relaunch

docs.title: Data rate lower than configured
docs.text:
Possible reasons:

  1. Hardware limitation: Each sensor has a maximum rate, and the device may not reach it
  2. IMU, Magnetometer: 100 Hz max
  3. Camera, LiDAR: 60 Hz max (30 Hz default); higher resolutions lower the achievable rate
  4. GPS: 10 Hz max (1 Hz default); the GPS hardware may update less often

  5. See Sensors and topics for every sensor

  6. Network congestion: Local network can't handle bandwidth

  7. CPU load: iOS throttling due to thermal/battery

Solutions:

  • Reduce rates for non-critical sensors
  • Reduce number of active sensors
  • Check network bandwidth

docs.title: Timestamps seem incorrect
docs.text:
Check:

  1. System time: header.stamp is wall-clock time (seconds since the Unix epoch, like ROS time on the host). Ensure the iOS device clock is set automatically (iOS Settings → General → Date & Time → Set Automatically), and that the host's clock is synchronized too.

  2. AR-derived topics: LiDAR point clouds, depth images, Device Pose (Conduit 3) and the camera images in LiDAR mode carry the ARKit frame's capture time, not the publish time. Messages from the same frame share an identical stamp.

  3. Comparing with ros2 topic delay: a large or negative delay usually means the two clocks differ, not that the data is late.

docs.title: No topics appear when using DDS
docs.text:
Problem: App shows "Publishing" but ros2 topic list on the ROS 2 host returns nothing.

Solutions:

  1. Restart the cached ros2 daemon first — if you changed RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, or CYCLONEDDS_URI in this shell, the daemon is still running with the old context and will lie to you. Run ros2 daemon stop before any of the checks below. See ros2 CLI shows stale topics after changing RMW_IMPLEMENTATION or CYCLONEDDS_URI for the full failure mode.

  2. Verify RMW implementation: 

    echo $RMW_IMPLEMENTATION
# Must be: rmw_cyclonedds_cpp

  3. Check domain IDs match (0-232 valid range for DDS/RTPS): 

    echo $ROS_DOMAIN_ID
    Must match the Domain ID field in Conduit Settings.

  4. Verify network interface binding on iOS:

  5. Conduit Settings → Discovery → Network Interface must be en0 (WiFi) on iPhone and iPad (the default).

  6. "auto" can fail because iOS may select a cellular or VPN interface.

  7. Multicast blocked by WiFi AP:

  8. Many consumer access points enable "AP isolation" or drop multicast.
  9. Workaround: add peers on both sides. In Conduit, Settings → Discovery → Peers: add the ROS 2 host's IP address. On the host, add the iPhone's address (shown as This Device on the same page) to the Peers list in CYCLONEDDS_URI. With peers, Conduit uses unicast on top of multicast.

  10. The QR code script can add the iPhone as a peer on the host for you.

  11. Firewall on ROS 2 host:

  12. DDS uses UDP ports starting at 7400 + 250 * domain_id (for domain 0: 7400, 7401, 7410, 7411).
  13. Allow UDP on those ports, or disable the firewall for the test LAN.

docs.title: ros2 CLI shows stale topics after changing RMW_IMPLEMENTATION or CYCLONEDDS_URI
docs.text:
Problem: You switched transports (e.g. Zenoh → DDS) or updated CYCLONEDDS_URI (peers, interface, tracing), but ros2 topic list keeps returning the previous transport's results or an empty list.

Cause: The ros2 CLI talks to a long-lived background daemon (_ros2_daemon). The daemon is started with whatever RMW_IMPLEMENTATION / DDS config was in effect at first launch and caches its RMW context — later env-var changes in your shell are ignored until the daemon is restarted.

Fix: Stop the daemon, then let the next CLI invocation start a fresh one in the new environment:

export RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=123
export CYCLONEDDS_URI='<CycloneDDS>…</CycloneDDS>'

ros2 daemon stop
ros2 daemon start          # optional — `ros2 topic list` will also autostart it
ros2 topic list

Any time you change RMW_IMPLEMENTATION, ROS_DOMAIN_ID, CYCLONEDDS_URI, or the Peer list, re-run ros2 daemon stop before the next command. This also applies when switching back to rmw_zenoh_cpp.

docs.title: Topics appear but ros2 topic echo shows no data (DDS)
docs.text:
Problem: Discovery works but data does not flow.

Solutions:

  1. QoS mismatch: Conduit uses BestEffort reliability for high-rate sensors (IMU, camera). If your subscriber requests Reliable, it will not match. Use --qos-profile sensor_data or --qos-reliability best_effort on the subscriber: 

    ros2 topic echo /conduit/imu --qos-reliability best_effort

  2. CameraInfo reliability: CameraInfo uses BestEffort with TransientLocal (latchedBestEffort). Standard image_transport subscribers expect Reliable — override the subscriber QoS.

  3. Large messages (Camera, LiDAR): Add peers (Settings → Discovery → Peers) so data also goes over unicast. Fragmented RTPS data over consumer Wi-Fi multicast is unreliable — see known-issues.md.

  4. "Waiting for subscriber" on the sensor row: Publish only when subscribed (Settings → Publishing) is on and no subscription matches the topic. Check the subscriber's QoS (best effort, see item 1), or turn the setting off. See On-demand capture.

docs.title: Disconnect takes several seconds (DDS)
docs.text:
Problem: After you press Stop, it can take a few seconds before "Publishing" clears.

Expected behavior: Closing the DDS publishers and participant can take a moment. No action is needed. See known-issues.md.

docs.title: iOS cannot reach the ROS 2 host (DDS over LAN)
docs.text:
Problem: ping from iOS to host works, but DDS discovery fails.

Solutions:

  • Confirm both devices are on the same subnet; DDS default transport is UDP, which does not cross routers without configuration.
  • Corporate networks often block multicast and inter-client UDP. Use a dedicated test LAN or phone hotspot.
  • On macOS Docker Desktop, the Docker container cannot receive DDS from iOS because Docker Desktop does not provide true host networking. Run the subscriber on Linux, a Parallels VM, or natively on macOS instead.
